summary: Full published-paper reading and a section-by-section mathematical inventory, with explicit genericity/convention boundaries and source corrections. The routing closes the inventory but does not yet certify proof-input closure, split every bundled conclusion or finish each definition API; the extraction remains partial for the listed gaps.

items.name: Coefficient, root and Frobenius conventions
items.statement: Fix p, sufficiently large E/Qp, its integers O, uniformizer varpi and residue F. For the applications G=GLn and Op finite etale over Zp; J=Hom(Op,O), Gbold=Res(Op/Zp)G base changed to O, pi(lambda)_sigma=lambda_(sigma Frobenius^-1). Use eta=(n-1,...,0) in each embedding, h_lambda=max over all roots of <lambda,alpha^vee>, X0 the characters pairing zero with every root. HT(cyclotomic)=+1 and covariant period functors; filtration jumps have opposite signs. General root statements retain the split connected reductive setup and existence of eta specified in §1.8.1.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Extended affine Weyl datum
items.statement: Wa=root lattice semidirect W and Wtilde=X*(T) semidirect W act on V=X*(T) tensor R. A0 has 0<root-pairing<1 for every positive root. Omega=Stab(A0), Wtilde=Wa semidirect Omega. Wplus sends A0 into the dominant chamber, W1plus into a restricted alcove (simple-root pairings between0 and1); wh=w0 t_-eta. Retain the central directions of the apartment.
items.note: Route owner: RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Length, Bruhat and upper-arrow orders
items.statement: Extend affine Coxeter length by l(w delta)=l(w), delta in Omega. Bruhat and Jantzen upper-arrow orders compare w1 delta and w2 delta exactly when their Wa parts compare; distinct right Wa cosets are incomparable. A relation X<=Y or X upward Y between sets means all pairs compare. Define W_le_z={x:x<=z}. Upper-arrow is not silently identified with Bruhat outside its comparison theorem's hypotheses.
items.note: Route owner: RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Reduced products of affine elements
items.statement: For m>=1 and w1,...,wm in Wtilde, the displayed product is reduced when l(product wi)=sum l(wi); factors need not be simple reflections.
items.note: Route owner: RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Admissible set
items.statement: Adm(lambda)=union over finite Weyl w of {z:z<=t_(w lambda)} for lambda in X*(T).
items.note: Route owner: RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Regular alcoves and regular admissible elements
items.statement: The alpha-strip of index m is m< <x,alpha^vee> <m+1. An alcove is regular if it is contained in no positive-root critical strip of index0. An affine element is regular when its image of A0 is regular; Admreg(lambda) is the regular part of Adm(lambda).
items.note: Route owner: RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Opposed dominant factors are reduced
items.statement: For w1,w2 in Wplus, w2^-1 w0 w1 is a reduced product.
items.note: Route owner: RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Regular affine-element factorization
items.statement: Every regular affine element is w2^-1 w0 t_nu w1 for w1,w2 in W1plus and dominant nu; the data are unique up to the central X0 action described in the proof.
items.note: Route owner: RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Converse regularity
items.statement: For any w1,w2 in Wplus, w2^-1 w0 w1 is regular.
items.note: Route owner: RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Admissibility and upper-arrow criterion
items.statement: For dominant lambda and w1,w2 in Wplus, the following are equivalent: w1 upward t_lambda wh^-1 w2; w2 upward wh t_-lambda w1; z=w2^-1 w0 w1 lies below BOTH t_(barw1^-1(lambda+eta)) and t_((w0 barw2)^-1(lambda+eta)); z belongs to Adm(lambda+eta). Bars mean finite Weyl images. This item needs separation into four implication leaves at blueprint time.
items.note: Route owner: RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Admissible pairs
items.statement: AP(lambda+eta) consists of pairs (w1,w2) in W1plus times Wplus modulo the diagonal central X0 action, satisfying w1 upward t_lambda wh^-1 w2, for dominant lambda.
items.note: Route owner: RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Admissible-pair parametrization
items.statement: For dominant lambda, (w1,w2) maps to w2^-1 w0 w1 and gives a bijection AP(lambda+eta) -> Admreg(lambda+eta).
items.note: Route owner: RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Reversed restricted-factor parametrization
items.statement: The same bijection holds for pairs in Wplus times W1plus modulo X0 with the same upper-arrow relation; the formula for the affine element is unchanged.
items.note: Route owner: RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Dual affine opposition map
items.statement: The target Wtilde-dual has the same group law but Bruhat order based at the antidominant alcove. Define (t_nu w)^*=w^-1 t_nu. It is an order equivalence and reverses products: (xy)^*=y^*x^*. The printed group-isomorphism assertion needs correction E1; use the opposite group for a multiplicative equivalence.
items.note: Route owner: RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Alcove depth
items.statement: A weight lambda is m-deep in an eta-shifted p-alcove with strip indices n_alpha if n_alpha p+m < <lambda+eta,alpha^vee> < (n_alpha+1)p-m. For m>=0, being m-deep in some alcove is equivalent to m<abs(<lambda+eta,alpha^vee>+pk) for all positive roots alpha and integers k.
items.note: Route owner: RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Affine genericity and smallness
items.statement: For z=w t_nu in either affine group, m-generic means nu-eta is m-deep, and m-small means h_nu<=m. Keep this right-translation convention; converting t_nu w uses the finite Weyl action.
items.note: Route owner: RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Polynomial genericity
items.statement: For P in Z[X1,...,Xn] and a in R^n, P-generic means P(a) modulo p is a unit in R/p. For a tuple indexed by finite J require this in every factor. This condition is generally not preserved by Weyl or dot actions.
items.note: Route owner: RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Genericity and smallness transport
items.statement: For nu a weight and every finite Weyl s, t_nu is m-generic (respectively m-small) iff t_(s nu) is; depth is invariant under the p-dot action and smallness under the ordinary Weyl action.
items.note: Route owner: RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Smallness under products
items.statement: If w is m-small and z is m'-small then wz is (m+m')-small, in either affine group.
items.note: Route owner: RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Smallness under inversion and opposition
items.statement: w is m-small iff w^-1 is m-small iff w^* is m-small.
items.note: Route owner: RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Loss of genericity under a small factor
items.statement: If z is m'-generic and w is m-small with m<=m', then zw is (m'-m)-generic.
items.note: Route owner: RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Integral highest-weight and virtual Weyl modules
items.statement: For dominant lambda, W(lambda)_O=Ind_B^G(w0 lambda), its E fibre is irreducible of highest weight lambda, and L(lambda) is the socle of its F fibre. For arbitrary lambda use the alternating derived-induction class sum_i(-1)^i R^i Ind_B^G(w0 lambda). V(lambda) is the restriction of the E module to G0(Zp), and W(lambda) the restriction of the F module to G0(Fp); distinguish genuine modules from virtual classes.
items.note: Route owner: PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Serre weights and restricted highest weights
items.statement: A Serre weight is an irreducible F-representation of G0(Fp). In the paper's finite reductive-group setup, write F(lambda)=L(lambda) restricted to G0(Fp) for lambda in X1={0<=simple-root pairing<=p-1}. Classes are parametrized by X1/(p-pi)X0. Regular means all these pairings are strictly less than p-1; m-depth is that of lambda. Coefficient F is sufficiently large for absolute irreducibility and definition of every weight.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Shifted p-alcoves and dot action
items.statement: For z=w t_nu define z dot lambda=w(lambda+eta+p nu)-eta. The shifted p-alcoves are components of the complement of H_(alpha,pn)-eta. C0 has 0<
items.note: Route owner: RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Constituent depth bound
items.statement: If dominant mu is not m-deep, h is an integer bounding <mu,alpha^vee> for every root, and sigma is a Jordan–Hölder factor of W(mu), then sigma is not (m+floor(h/(p-1)))-deep. Proof uses linkage, Steinberg tensor product, tensor-weight translation, convexity and a terminating height reduction; none may be replaced by an assumed constituent classification.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Dominant translate remains in a Weyl polytope
items.statement: If lambda is dominant, nu is in Conv(W kappa), and w(lambda+nu) is dominant, then w(lambda+nu)-lambda lies in Conv(W kappa). The proof moves across root walls and keeps each corrected nu on a segment between two Weyl conjugates.
items.note: Route owner: RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Algebraic and finite central characters
items.statement: Algebraic central characters are X*(Z), finite central characters X*(Z)/(p-pi)X*(Z), identified with Hom(Z0(Fp),F^times). F(lambda) has central character lambda restricted to Z modulo (p-pi). Identify X*(Z) with Wtilde/Wa where the source uses this identification.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Lowest-alcove presentation of a Serre weight
items.statement: For omega-eta in C0 and w1 in W1plus put F_(w1,omega)=F(pi^-1(w1) dot (omega-eta)). Quotient pairs by (w1,omega)~(t_nu w1,omega-nu) for nu in X0. A presentation is this equivalence class, not a unique unquotiented pair.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Compatibility of Serre-weight presentations
items.statement: The algebraic central lift of (w1,omega) is the image of t_(omega-eta) w1 in Wtilde/Wa=X*(Z). Compatible presentations have the same such lift; this is independent of the chosen representative pair.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Central character of a lowest-alcove presentation
items.statement: The lift in(2.7) reduces modulo(p-pi) to the central character of F_(w1,omega).
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Presentations classified by central lifts
items.statement: For a0-deep Serre weight sigma, (w1,omega) maps to the class of t_(omega-eta)w1 and bijects its lowest-alcove presentations with algebraic lifts of its finite central character. The printed formula omits -eta; retaining it would change the target character.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Deligne–Lusztig representations
items.statement: For a good pair(s,mu) in W times X*(T), attach the E-representation R_s(mu) of G0(Fp), using the Deligne–Lusztig construction and the sign convention of the cited inputs. A lowest-alcove presentation is(s,mu-eta) with mu-eta in C0; good-pair construction is an external prerequisite, not a formal symbol.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Generic Deligne–Lusztig presentation
items.statement: R is m-generic if it has a lowest-alcove presentation(s,mu-eta) of depth m. After choosing it, wtilde(R)=t_mu s and w(R)=s; an unchosen representation has no distinguished such element.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Generic Deligne–Lusztig irreducibility
items.statement: A1-generic Deligne–Lusztig representation is irreducible; a0-deep lowest-alcove pair is good. Inputs are[19] Theorem6.8 and[56] Lemma2.2.3.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Central compatibility of Deligne–Lusztig presentations
items.statement: A presentation(s,mu-eta) is lambda-compatible with zeta if t_lambda t_mu s has class zeta in Wtilde/Wa. Compatibility with a Serre presentation uses its lift from(2.7). The finite central character of R tensor W(lambda) is zeta modulo(p-pi).
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Deligne–Lusztig presentations and central lifts
items.statement: For1-generic R, (s,mu-eta) maps to t_mu s modulo Wa and bijects its lowest-alcove presentations with algebraic lifts of its reduced finite central character.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: A bounded presentation for every Deligne–Lusztig representation
items.statement: Every R has R=R_s(mu) with mu dominant and h_mu<=p+2; consequently mu-eta is(-3)-deep in C0. For products of GLn the stronger(-1)-depth is available as Remark2.3.5 records, but needs its own justification.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Deep constituents force generic types
items.statement: For dominant lambda with h_(lambda+eta)<p-3, if JH(Rbar tensor W(lambda)) contains an m-deep weight, then R admits(s,mu) with mu-eta(m-h_(lambda+2eta))-deep in C0. In the GLn-product refinement one may replace p-3 by p-1.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Jantzen constituent criterion
items.statement: For a2h_eta-generic presentation(s,mu-eta) of R and lambda in X1, F(lambda) belongs to JH(Rbar) iff some z=w t_nu in Wplus satisfies z dot(mu-s pi(nu)-eta) upward wh dot lambda and z dot C0 upward wh dot C0.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Admissible-pair parametrization of tensor constituents
items.statement: For dominant lambda, m>=max(2h_eta,h_(lambda+eta)), and a chosen m-generic presentation of R, (w1,w2) maps to F_(w1,wtilde(R)w2^-1(0)) and bijects AP(lambda+eta) with JH(Rbar tensor W(lambda)). These are sets of constituents; this does not assert multiplicity one.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Depth and central compatibility of tensor constituents
items.statement: With the hypotheses of N40, every constituent is(m-h_(lambda+eta))-deep, and its displayed lowest-alcove presentation is lambda-compatible with that of R.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Constituents by translated Bruhat intervals
items.statement: For dominant lambda, lambda-compatible lowest-alcove presentations(w1,omega) of sigma and(s,mu-eta) of R, and R max(2h_eta,h_(lambda+eta))-generic, sigma lies in JH(Rbar tensor W(lambda)) iff t_omega W_le_(w0 w1) is contained in t_mu s Adm(lambda+eta).
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Outer constituents
items.statement: For R max(2h_eta,h_(lambda+eta))-generic, JHout(Rbar tensor W(lambda)) is the subset under N40 corresponding to pairs(w1,wh t_-lambda w1).
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Outer constituent controls upper-arrow inequalities
items.statement: If F_(w',omega') is outer in Rbar and(w,omega) is a compatible presentation of any constituent in Rbar, then w upward t_(barw' barw(R)^-1(omega'-omega)) w'. Here the action on the difference uses the finite Weyl part; representatives may be chosen arbitrarily within the compatible classes.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Covering relation on Serre weights
items.statement: A3h_eta-deep weight sigma0 covers sigma if every2h_eta-generic Deligne–Lusztig representation whose reduction contains sigma0 also contains sigma. This is an intersection condition over all such R.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Covering criterion by alcove inequalities
items.statement: For compatible presentations(w,omega),(w',omega') with omega-eta3h_eta-deep, F_(w,omega) covers F_(w',omega') iff w' upward t_(s(omega-omega')) w for every s in W. Consequently l(w')<=l(w), with equality iff the presentations are equivalent.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Covering criterion by intervals
items.statement: Under N46's hypotheses, covering is equivalent to t_omega' W_le_(w0 w') being contained in t_omega W_le_(w0 w).
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Covering criterion by algebraic modules
items.statement: Under N46's hypotheses, covering is equivalent to F_(w',omega') occurring in the restriction to G0(Fp) of the direct sum of L(pi^-1(w1) dot(omega-eta)) over w1 in Wplus with w1 upward w. On3h_eta-deep weights this gives a partial order, with antisymmetry from the length equality criterion.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Tame inertial L-parameters from Weyl data
items.statement: For(w,mu), set Fstar=p pi^-1 on the dual cocharacter lattice and choose d with(Fstar w^-1)^d=p^d. Evaluate the cocharacter sum_(i=0)^(d-1)(Fstar w^-1)^i(mu) on the fundamental character omega_d. The conjugacy class tau(w,mu) is independent of d and every tame inertial L-parameter arises thus. Reduction and Teichmuller lift biject the O,E,F versions.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Explicit tame inertia characters for GLn
items.statement: For unramified K/Qp of degree f and(s,mu+eta), s_tau=s0...s_(f-1), r=ord(s_tau), alpha_j=s_(f-1)^-1...s_(f-j)^-1(mu_(f-j)+eta_(f-j)), a0=sum_(j=0)^(f-1)p^j alpha_j. The type is the direct sum over i of omega_(fr) raised to sum_(k=0)^(r-1)p^(fk) a0_(s_tau^k(i)). It is independent of the algebraic-closure isomorphism used to derive the formula.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Lowest-alcove presentations and the E/F central shift
items.statement: A presentation(s,mu) has mu in C0 and tau=tau(s,mu+eta). For E-valued tau, lambda-compatibility uses t_lambda t_(mu+eta)s modulo Wa. For F-valued bartau, compatibility uses t_mu s modulo Wa. Reduction therefore changes the compatible central lift by -eta restricted to Z; do not identify the two conventions.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Regular and generic tame types
items.statement: Regular means each coroot evaluated on a torus-valued conjugate is nontrivial. m-generic means a lowest-alcove presentation(s,mu) with mu m-deep exists. With a chosen presentation set wtilde(tau)=t_(mu+eta)s. These notions apply to F types as well. One-generic implies regular; having a lowest-alcove presentation is equivalent to0-genericity.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Characteristic-zero types and determinant lifts
items.statement: For1-generic tau over E, (s,mu) maps to t_(mu+eta)s modulo Wa and bijects lowest-alcove presentations with zeta in X*(Z) satisfying zeta composed with omega1=det tau.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Residual types and determinant lifts
items.locator: Lemma2.4.4, second part, PDF48, corrected E3
items.statement: For1-generic bartau, the map(s,mu)->t_mu s modulo Wa bijects lowest-alcove presentations with zeta such that(zeta+eta restricted to Z) composed with baromega1=det bartau. The printed minus sign contradicts the definition of tau(s,mu+eta).
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Changing a diagonal tame presentation
items.statement: For z=t_nu w, omega a weight and kappa=pi^-1(z) dot(omega-eta), tau(1,kappa) is isomorphic to tau(pi^-1(w)^-1 w, omega+pi^-1(w)^-1(nu-eta)).
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Weil–Deligne inertial parameter
items.statement: A pair(rho_tau,N_tau) consists of an open-kernel inertia homomorphism and a nilpotent Lie element, admitting a Weil extension with Ad(rho(g))N_tau=norm(g)N_tau; take conjugacy classes, and for L-parameters require the prescribed projection to the Galois factor. For a local field K use its Weil group and its residue cardinality in the norm. Tameness concerns rho_tau, and an ordinary inertial type is the N_tau=0 subcase.
items.note: Route owner: SmoothRepresentationsPartII. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Monodromy dominance on inertial types
items.statement: For GLn compare nilpotent conjugacy classes by dominance of their Jordan partitions. Put tau<=tau' when their inertia representations agree and the nilpotent restrictions to every irreducible inertia-isotypic summand compare in this order; for collections compare componentwise. Zero monodromy is minimal.
items.note: Route owner: SmoothRepresentationsPartII. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Occurrence of an inertial type bounds monodromy
items.statement: For any WD inertial type tau of GLn(K) there exists smooth irreducible sigma(tau) of GLn(OK) over sufficiently large E such that its occurrence in an irreducible admissible pi implies rec_K(pi) restricted to inertia <=tau. No uniqueness of sigma(tau) is asserted.
items.note: Route owner: SmoothRepresentationsPartII. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Exact inertial type has multiplicity one
items.statement: For the sigma(tau) supplied in N58, rec_K(pi) restricted to inertia=tau implies multiplicity one of sigma(tau) in pi restricted to GLn(OK).
items.note: Route owner: SmoothRepresentationsPartII. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Generic representations and dominated monodromy
items.statement: For the same sigma(tau), if pi is generic and rec_K(pi) restricted to inertia<=tau, then sigma(tau) occurs; its multiplicity is one if additionally tau is maximal in the monodromy order.
items.note: Route owner: SmoothRepresentationsPartII. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Tame types are constituents of Deligne–Lusztig representations
items.statement: For G=GLn and(s,mu), one can choose the sigma(tau) of N58 as tau=(tau(s,mu),N_tau) varies so that their set is exactly the irreducible constituents of R_s(mu), inflated to GLn(Op). The proof uses cuspidal types, Bernstein covers and parabolic induction; it does not assert an arbitrary previously chosen sigma has this property.
items.note: Route owner: SmoothRepresentationsPartII. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Herzig involution and predicted weights
items.statement: For regular sigma=F(lambda), define R(sigma)=F(wh dot lambda); this is well defined and bijective, with square a character twist. For tame bartau put W?(bartau)=R(JH(sigma([bartau]))), with the regular-weight domain understood as in Herzig's recipe and the generic range used subsequently; [bartau] denotes Teichmuller lift.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Parametrization of Herzig weights
items.statement: For m>=2h_eta and a chosen m-generic presentation of bartau, pairs(w,w2) in W1plus times Wplus modulo diagonal X0 with w2 upward w map bijectively to W?(bartau) by F_(w,wtilde(bartau)w2^-1(0)).
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Depth and compatibility of Herzig weights
items.statement: With N63's hypotheses all the displayed weights are(m-h_eta)-deep and their presentations are compatible with the F-valued presentation of bartau.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Obvious Serre weights
items.statement: Wobv(bartau) is the subset in N63 given by pairs(w,w). Such a weight is determined by the finite Weyl image of w, retaining the presentation convention.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Relative position of residual and lifted types
items.statement: For lambda-compatible chosen presentations of rhobar over F and tau over E, define wtilde(rhobar,tau)=wtilde(tau)^-1 wtilde(rhobar). It is presentation-dependent data with the specified compatibility, not an invariant without choices.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Breuil–Mézard weight-intersection criterion
items.statement: For dominant lambda and lambda-compatible2h_eta-generic rhobar and max(2h_eta,h_(lambda+eta))-generic tau presentations, a compatible(w,omega) represents a weight in W?(rhobar) intersect JH(sigma(tau)bar tensor W(lambda)) iff there are w1,w2 in Wplus with w1 upward w upward t_lambda wh^-1 w2 and omega=wtilde(rhobar)w1^-1(0)=wtilde(tau)w2^-1(0). The tensor factor is omitted in the printed first assertion.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Affine factorization of equal weight parameters
items.statement: In N67's setup, equality of the two expressions for omega holds iff wtilde(rhobar,tau)=w2^-1 s w1 for some finite Weyl s.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Extremal intersection is a single obvious weight
items.statement: Under N67's hypotheses, if wtilde(rhobar,tau)=t_(s^-1(lambda+eta)) for finite Weyl s, then W?(rhobar) intersect JH(sigma(tau)bar tensor W(lambda)) consists of exactly the obvious weight corresponding to s. In the proof the forced equality is w=w1, not the printed w=w2 (E5).
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Admissibility produces an obvious common weight
items.statement: Under N67's genericity and compatibility hypotheses, if wtilde(rhobar,tau) belongs to Adm(lambda+eta), then Wobv(rhobar) intersect JH(sigma(tau)bar tensor W(lambda)) is nonempty.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Herzig weights lie in one auxiliary tensor type
items.statement: For a3h_eta-generic chosen bartau presentation, take the eta-compatible Deligne–Lusztig representation R with wtilde(R)=wtilde(bartau)t_(-eta-w0 eta). Then W?(bartau) is contained in JH(Rbar tensor W(eta)); -eta-w0 eta is central.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Universal Iwahori group scheme
items.statement: Over X=Spec Z[v], construct the smooth affine Bruhat–Tits group scheme G with connected fibres from cyclic n-tuples of invertible matrices satisfying D_i A_(i-1)=A_i D_i, where D_i has v in its ith diagonal position. If v maps to a regular element t in R, its R-points are the invertible matrices upper triangular modulo t. Use the tuple functor for arbitrary bases.
items.note: Route owner: GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Universal positive and full loop groups
items.statement: At v->t in a Noetherian ring R, L+G(R)=G(R[[v-t]]) and LG(R)=G(R((v-t))), using the map that sends v to the formal variable v inside these rings. They are represented by a scheme and an ind-group scheme. For Noetherian R use matrices upper triangular modulo v; v is regular in these completed rings. T maps in by constant diagonal matrices, and determinant takes values in the Gm loop group.
items.note: Route owner: GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Universal affine Grassmannian and bounded pieces
items.statement: The fpqc quotient L+G\LG is represented by an ind-projective X-ind-scheme Gr. Its fibre off v=0 is the GLn affine Grassmannian and at0 the standard Iwahori affine flag variety. LGdet=d requires det(A)=(v-t)^d times a power-series unit. L+M consists of matrices over R[[v-t]] upper triangular modulo v. Bound A by (v-t)^-h L+M, h>=0; its determinant-d quotient is projective over X and exhausts the determinant-d piece as h grows. Quotients of R-points inject into sheaf-quotient points, not necessarily surject.
items.note: Route owner: GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Negative loop subgroup
items.statement: L--G consists of invertible matrices polynomial in(v-t)^-1, lower unipotent at(v-t)^-1=0 and upper triangular modulo v/(v-t). The positive, full and negative loop groups are formally smooth over X in the source's Noetherian test-ring setting.
items.note: Route owner: GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Unique positive-negative factorization
items.statement: Multiplication L+G times_X L--G -> LG is a monomorphism. Consequently L--G -> Gr is a monomorphism. Proof uses intersections of nonnegative and strictly negative Laurent degrees and v-regularity.
items.note: Route owner: GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Square-zero loop Lie modules
items.statement: For R->S with square-zero kernel J, define Lie LG(J), Lie L+G(J), Lie L--G(J) by the corresponding matrix-entry and triangular conditions with coefficients J. M->1+M identifies these with the respective congruence kernels; conjugation factors through the S-valued group.
items.note: Route owner: GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Positive-negative Lie splitting
items.statement: For a square-zero extension of Noetherian Z[v]-algebras with kernel J, Lie LG(J)=Lie L--G(J) direct-sum Lie L+G(J), using Laurent positive/negative decomposition separately in upper and v-divisible lower entries.
items.note: Route owner: GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Artinian formal etaleness at a point
items.statement: A morphism of functors on Noetherian rings is formally etale at x:Spec k->F in this section if every compatible Artinian local thickening Spec A->G with residue field k admits a unique lift to F. For representable locally finite-type morphisms with locally Noetherian target this implies etaleness; it is deliberately weaker than the unrestricted formal-lifting definition.
items.note: Route owner: SchemeAndStackFoundations. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Formal etaleness of loop factorization
items.statement: L+G times_X L--G -> LG and L--G -> Gr are formally etale in U08's sense. Lift across successive square-zero ideals using formal smoothness, then correct by U07; uniqueness comes from U05.
items.note: Route owner: GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Affine-element chart functor
items.statement: For z=w t_nu in the dual affine group, U(z) consists of A for which A(v-t)^-nu w^-1 is polynomial in(v-t)^-1 and lower unipotent modulo(v-t)^-1, and A(v-t)^-nu is upper triangular modulo v/(v-t). It is a subfunctor of LG. Its bounded determinant part intersects LGdet=sum(nu),<=h.
items.note: Route owner: GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Chart torsor and formal etaleness
items.statement: Left multiplication makes U(z) an L--G torsor, and U(z)->Gr is a formally etale monomorphism. Point sets may be empty over a given base; no global trivialization is presumed.
items.note: Route owner: GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Explicit bounded chart equations
items.statement: For Noetherian R, A in U(w t_nu)det,<=h has A_ij=v^[i>j] sum_(k=-h)^(nu_j-[i>j]-[i<w(j)]) c_(ij,k)(v-t)^k, pivot c_(w(j)j,nu_j-[w(j)>j])=1, and det A=det(w)(v-t)^sum(nu). Empty coefficient ranges contribute zero. These equations represent the chart by a finite-type affine scheme. Do not impose a nonemptiness inequality on every nonpivot entry: the sentence following the proposition is too strong (source issue E7).
items.note: Route owner: GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Distinguished chart section
items.statement: For a nonempty bounded chart, its v=0 fibre has a section over Z represented by w v^nu. Distinguish this section from a choice of an arbitrary matrix representative over nonzero v.
items.note: Route owner: GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Bounded charts are open
items.statement: U(z)det,<=h -> Grdet=sum(nu),<=h is an open immersion, via finite type plus formal etaleness and monomorphism.
items.note: Route owner: GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Universal differential condition
items.statement: LGnabla is the subfunctor of LG times An of pairs(g,a) with v g' g^-1 + Ad(g)Diag(a) in(v-t)^-1 L+M. Its left L+G invariance makes the quotient a closed sub-ind-scheme Grnabla of Gr times An, ind-proper over X times An. A common scalar shift of all coordinates of a yields the isomorphism in Remark3.3.2 with the hyperplane a_n=0 times A1.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Descent of the differential condition
items.statement: For h in L+G, v(hg)'(hg)^-1+Ad(hg)D=v h'h^-1+Ad(h)(v g'g^-1+Ad(g)D), which lies in(v-t)^-1 L+M whenever the original expression does. The printed calculation and claim h' in L+M are corrected in E12; the integral term is v h'.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Global Schubert variety and orbit projection
items.statement: s_lambda is represented by(v-t)^lambda. SX(lambda) is the irreducible closed right-L+G-stable orbit closure; its open stratum excludes smaller dominant weights in the Weyl polytope. Off v=0, the orbit quotient L+G_lambda\L+G identifies with this stratum and maps to P_lambda\GLn by reduction modulo(v-t); the map is an iterated affine-space bundle. P_lambda has vanishing root entries where <lambda,alpha^vee><0.
items.note: Route owner: GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Naive universal local model
items.statement: Mnv_X(<=lambda,nabla)=Grnabla intersect(SX(lambda) times An). Its chart Unv(z,<=lambda,nabla) is the intersection with U(z) times An, equal to the sufficiently bounded-chart intersection.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Open differential stratum is a flag variety
items.statement: For dominant lambda, after inverting h_lambda!, the orbit projection identifies Mnv_X0 intersect(Sopen_X0(lambda) times An) with(P_lambda\GLn) times X0 times An. The triangular recursion solves positive Laurent coefficients from constant coefficients using invertibility of t and integers1,...,h_lambda.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Reduced generic universal decomposition
items.statement: After inverting h_lambda!, the reduced Mnv_X0(<=lambda,nabla) is the disjoint union of(P_lambda'\GLn) times X0 times An for dominant lambda'<=lambda. Keep the localization; the proof removes each open proper component successively.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Universal local model as a closure
items.statement: MX(lambda,nabla) is the closure of the lambda open differential stratum over X0 inside the naive universal model (equivalently inside Gr times An). Imposing the differential equation before closure differs from imposing it after closure. A later flatness/base-change argument is needed to identify specializations with closures formed after specializing.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Torus fixed points of global Schubert varieties
items.statement: Over X0 the torus-fixed subscheme of SX(lambda) is supported on sections s_mu for integral mu in the Weyl polytope Conv(lambda); this is a support assertion, not an assertion that the fixed scheme is reduced.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Generic universal naive model is smooth
items.statement: For dominant lambda, Mnv_X0(<=lambda,nabla) becomes smooth over X0 times An after inverting(2h_lambda)!. Proof reduces to torus-fixed points by properness of the non-smooth locus, then bounds diagonal and root tangent coefficients by the displayed recursion. Combined with U20 it removes the reduction qualification in that decomposition after this stronger localization.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Elkik lifting for a fixed chart presentation
items.statement: Fix lambda,z and a finite presentation of Unv(z,<=lambda,nabla)[1/(2h_lambda)!] over X times An. There are N>2r and r depending on the presentation such that, for any t-adically complete t-torsion-free ring A with a base map v->t, every compatible A/t^m point with m>=N lifts to an A point agreeing modulo t^(m-r). No uniqueness or agreement modulo t^m is claimed; the torsion-free hypothesis is required by the cited Elkik lemma.
items.note: Route owner: SchemeAndStackFoundations. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Equal-characteristic closure model
items.statement: For a field k with(2h_lambda)! invertible and a in k^n, first specialize the naive family at a and then take the closure of its lambda flag component over X0_k; call this M(lambda,nabla_a). It is flat over A1_k. The map to MX(lambda,nabla) specialized at a is an isomorphism over X0, but need not be an isomorphism on the whole fibre without a generic-base-change argument.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Unibranch points and normalization
items.statement: A point y is unibranch when the normalization of the reduced local ring is local. Under finite normalization its fibre is then a single point, equivalently connected. For a REDUCED excellent Noetherian local ring, unibranchness is equivalent to its completion being a domain. The printed remark omits reducedness (source issue E9); dual numbers show why it is necessary.
items.note: Route owner: SchemeAndStackFoundations. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Extended torus and chart action
items.statement: Tdual times Gm acts on the universal Grassmannian by right diagonal multiplication and loop rotation v->r^-1v, with the induced scaling of t. On the z=w t_nu chart the representative formula is(D,r)A=Ad(w)(D^-1) A(r^-1v) r^nu D. It preserves the chart and all its bounded pieces and makes the chart map equivariant.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Contracting chart action
items.statement: Choose regular dominant mu and N>h_mu. The one-parameter subgroup r->(Ad(w^-1)(r^mu),r^N) gives a contracting action on every bounded z chart and has distinguished section z as its fixed subscheme when nonempty. Direct substitution in U27 gives coefficient weight N(nu_j-[i>j]-k)+mu_(w(j))-mu_i. The proof prints the opposite mu-signs (source issue E8); with the corrected weights all nonpivot variables have positive weight.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Contraction gives a unibranch vertex
items.statement: For an irreducible variety M over an algebraically closed field with an A1 multiplicative-monoid action whose unique Gm-fixed point is x, M is unibranch at x and its completed local ring is a domain. Normalize, lift the action, and use the0-action map to show the finite normalization fibre is connected. Reducedness comes from the variety hypothesis.
items.note: Route owner: SchemeAndStackFoundations. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Equal-characteristic unibranchness after power base change
items.statement: Under U25's hypotheses, if z_k lies in M(lambda,nabla_a), then for every integer e>0 its base change under v->v^e is unibranch at z_k. The preimage of the z chart in the normalization's v=0 fibre is connected. The contraction lifts after composing its scaling cocharacter with the e-power map.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Normalization fibres in a flat family
items.statement: For the universal family restricted to U in An and its e-power base change, assume both M_U and the normalization of M_U,e in its X0 part are flat over X times U. At a geometric special-fibre point in a distinguished z section, the normalization fibre is supported at one point; the normalization preimage of the z chart in that fibre is connected. Both flatness hypotheses are retained.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Flatness across a principal divisor
items.statement: For an A[v]-algebra B, if v is regular in B, B[1/v] is flat over A[v,1/v], and B/v is flat over A, then B is flat over A[v], in the local-criterion setting used by the finite-presentation family. Before stating this for unrestricted B, audit the cited local flatness criterion's finiteness hypotheses.
items.note: Route owner: SchemeAndStackFoundations. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Generic flatness of a closure family
items.statement: For integral finite-type Z-scheme S and finite-presentation M->X times S, if v is regular on M and M restricted to X0 is flat over X0 times S, then after restricting to a nonempty open U in S the whole family is flat. Apply generic flatness to the v=0 fibre and U32.
items.note: Route owner: SchemeAndStackFoundations. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Geometrically S1 special fibres after shrinking
items.statement: In Setup3.5.1 (S integral finite type with characteristic-zero generic point, M finitely presented, normal, closure of its smooth X0 part), additionally assume flatness over X times S. After shrinking S nontrivially, the v=0 fibres are geometrically S1. First spread geometric normality of M's generic fibre over S; quotient by the regular element v.
items.note: Route owner: SchemeAndStackFoundations. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Codimension-one regularity under uniformizer specialization
items.statement: In Setup3.5.1 with flatness, there is a nonempty etale U->S such that a DVR map Spec R->X times U sending v to a uniformizer yields an R1 base change M_R. Spread geometric integrality of special components and their principal generators in height-one localizations; the displayed base arrows in the printed statement need correction to X times U and Spec R.
items.note: Route owner: SchemeAndStackFoundations. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Normality spreads to generic DVR specializations
items.statement: In Setup3.5.1 there is a nonempty open U in S such that for every complete DVR R and map Spec R->X times U sending v to a UNIFORMIZER, M_R is flat over R and normal. Combine U33,U34,U35 and Serre R1+S2. In the proof, an etale lift may require a faithfully flat unramified DVR extension; completeness alone does not supply a residue-field point. Normality then descends. The unrestricted higher-valuation claim is false, as x^2-v with v->varpi^2 shows.
items.note: Route owner: SchemeAndStackFoundations. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Quasi-finite horizontal subscheme through a section
items.statement: Let M->X times S be flat finite type between finite-type Z-schemes, with S irreducible and characteristic-zero generic point, and s:S->M0 a section. There is a nonempty open U in S and a closed Z in M restricted over X times U, flat and quasi-finite over X times U, containing s restricted to U. The proof needs a horizontal curve through the generic section point, then spreading and generic flatness.
items.note: Route owner: SchemeAndStackFoundations. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Uniform bounded-extension lift of a section
items.statement: Under U37's hypotheses there are e and nonempty open U such that for any complete DVR R mapping to X times U with v of positive valuation, the point induced by s lifts after a finite DVR extension R'/R of degree<=e. Use the finite flat connected piece of the quasi-finite horizontal subscheme and normalize it.
items.note: Route owner: SchemeAndStackFoundations. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Product universal local model
items.statement: For finite J and dominant tuple lambda, take the product over the common X of MX(lambda_j,nabla), with parameters in(An)^J. Distinguished sections and charts are products indexed by z in Wtilde-dual^J. The shared X coordinate is not duplicated into independent deformation parameters.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Uniform unibranchness for product specializations
items.statement: Fix e>0, n and a finite set of dominant cocharacters. There is a nonempty open U in An depending only on this set,e,n such that, for every finite tuple drawn from the set, complete DVR R and map Spec R->X times U^J sending v to an element of positive valuation<=e, the specialized product model is R-flat and unibranch at each special-fibre point on a distinguished section z. The v-unit case has no such special distinguished points.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Integral adic chart domain for product models
items.statement: Under U40's hypotheses, for a distinguished section z meeting the special fibre, the maximal-ideal-of-R-adic completion of the coordinate ring of its chart in the specialized product is a domain. This is completion of the whole affine chart along the base ideal, not merely its completed local ring at z.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Normalization connectivity controls adic completion
items.statement: For a complete DVR R and finite-type flat R-algebra A with A[1/varpi] a regular domain, if Spec(A^normal/varpi) is connected, then the varpi-adic completion of A is a domain. Finiteness of normalization and excellence give an injection into a normal completed algebra; any nontrivial idempotent there would survive reduction, contradicting connectedness.
items.note: Route owner: DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Geometric connectedness input for products of charts
items.locator: Theorem3.7.1 proof, PDF79–80; [10] LemmaA.1.1 and [54] Proposition2.2
items.statement: The proof requires domain results for completed tensor products over a complete DVR: factors have a rational point and regular generic fibre. It uses geometric connectedness of a regular affinoid domain with a rational point, and regularity of the product. Exact external statements and the claimed extension of[54] beyond finite extensions of Zp remain a prerequisite-reading gate; do not replace them by the false assertion that arbitrary tensor products of domains are domains.
items.note: Route owner: DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Pappas–Zhu GLn Iwahori local model
items.statement: Specialize the universal loop construction at t=-p over O. The generic fibre is the GLn affine Grassmannian and the special fibre the Iwahori affine flag variety. For dominant lambda, M(<=lambda) is the closure of the generic Schubert variety through(v+p)^lambda. Its special fibre is the reduced union of cells indexed by Adm-dual(lambda), by Pappas–Zhu9.3 and coherence; this reducedness is not inherited by its differential intersections.
items.note: Route owner: GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Mixed-characteristic differential locus
items.statement: For a in O^n, require v A'A^-1+Ad(A)Diag(a) in(v+p)^-1 L+M_O. Its left-positive-loop quotient Grnabla_a is closed in Gr_O and is the fibre of the universal differential locus at(-p,a).
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Generic differential stratum is a smooth flag variety
items.statement: For any a in O^n, Sopen_E(lambda) intersect Grnabla_a is naturally(P_lambda\GLn)_E. It is closed in the generic Schubert closure, irreducible, projective and smooth.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Flat monodromy local model
items.statement: M(lambda,nabla_a) is the closure of M03 in M(<=lambda). It is projective, O-flat and of relative dimension dim(P_lambda\GLn), and must be distinguished from the naive intersection.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Naive mixed-characteristic local model
items.statement: Mnv(<=lambda,nabla_a)=M(<=lambda) intersect Grnabla_a. Via flatness of the global Schubert variety, it agrees with specialization of the naive universal model; this extra input is Richarz Theorem1.5 as cited in Remark4.1.4.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Union of flat Hodge-stratum closures
items.statement: For each dominant lambda'<=lambda, M(lambda',nabla_a) is a closed subscheme of Mnv(<=lambda,nabla_a). Their scheme-theoretic union M(<=lambda,nabla_a) is O-flat and projective.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Flat union and naive model have the same generic fibre
items.statement: M(<=lambda,nabla_a)_E=Mnv(<=lambda,nabla_a)_E, the reduced disjoint union of(P_lambda'\GLn)_E over dominant lambda'<=lambda. This proves no equality of the integral models or their special fibres.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Residue tuple genericity
items.statement: A tuple a in R^n for an F-algebra is m-generic when for i!=j its difference a_i-a_j avoids every integer in[-m,m] mapped into R. For integral nu whose translation is m-generic, nu modulo p satisfies this condition. In the affine-cell theorem R is F, so the avoided scalars are units when nonzero.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Differential affine-cell dimension
items.statement: For positive h, w in Wtilde h-small and a in O^n whose residue is h-generic, Sopen_F(w^*) intersect Flnabla_a is affine space of dimension d minus the number of positive-root critical strips containing w(A0), where d=dim(B\GLn). Proof eliminates all but the top coefficient in each supported root using scalar i+[alpha>0]+<a,alpha^vee>.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Smallness of admissible elements
items.statement: For w in Adm(lambda), w^* lies in Adm-dual(lambda) and is h_lambda-small.
items.note: Route owner: RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Top components of the naive special fibre
items.statement: For dominant lambda and residue a h_lambda-generic, closure of Sopen_F(w^*) intersect Flnabla_a gives a bijection from Admreg(lambda) to the d-dimensional irreducible components of Mnv(<=lambda,nabla_a)_F. Do not infer that the entire special fibre is reduced or equidimensional from this statement.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Affine root subgroup charts
items.statement: For GLn the affine root subgroup U_(alpha,m) has a single off-diagonal entry c v^m. If w=s t_nu and z=w^*, then z^-1 U_(-alpha,m) z=U_(-s(alpha),m+<nu,alpha^vee>). For x in A0, U_(-alpha,m) lies in z^-1 I z iff <w(x),alpha^vee><m, and in z^-1 L--G z iff m< <w(x),alpha^vee>.
items.note: Route owner: GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Unipotent affine-cell subgroup and support
items.statement: N_z=z^-1 L--G_F z intersect I_F. Its support is the set of finite roots alpha for which some U_(alpha,m) lies in N_z.
items.note: Route owner: GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Polynomial coordinates for the cell subgroup
items.statement: For z=w^* and x in A0, U_(-alpha,m) lies in N_z exactly when <x,alpha^vee><m< <w(x),alpha^vee>. Consequently the -alpha matrix entry is v^[alpha>0] f_alpha(v), where degree f_alpha<=d_(alpha,w)=floor(<w(x),alpha^vee>)-ceil(<x,alpha^vee>), and f=0 for d<0. The source's phrase 'has degree' must be read as a bound, since the identity has zero entries.
items.note: Route owner: GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Unipotent subgroup parametrizes the Schubert cell
items.statement: N_z is a finite-dimensional affine unipotent group scheme and z N_z -> Sopen_F(z) is an affine-space isomorphism of dimension l(z).
items.note: Route owner: GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Support criterion and count
items.statement: For w and x in A0, -alpha lies in Supp(N_w*) iff floor(<w(x),alpha^vee>)>=ceil(<x,alpha^vee>), equivalently <w(x),alpha^vee>>0 and x,w(x) lie in different alpha-strips. For the finite Weyl s with s^-1 w in Wplus, -Supp(N_w*) is contained in s(Phi+), and the support size is d minus the number of positive-root critical strips containing w(A0).
items.note: Route owner: GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Triangular cell subgroup
items.statement: For s in M16, N_w* lies in s(L+N)s^-1 where N is the lower unipotent subgroup. This gives the root partial order used in M09's triangular coefficient elimination.
items.note: Route owner: GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Common zero-parameter differential affine flag
items.statement: Flnabla0 is the fpqc sheafification of I A satisfying v A'A^-1 in v^-1 Lie I. It is the zero-parameter differential locus in Fl; use the explicit chosen affine Weyl embedding for right translations.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Translate differential models to the common flag
items.statement: For z=s^-1 t_mu in Wtilde-dual, a integral with a congruent to s^-1(mu) modulo p, right translation identifies Mnv(<=lambda,nabla_a)_F with M(<=lambda)_F z intersect Flnabla0. The same identity holds on each Schubert cell. Thus this right translation is a closed immersion of the naive special fibre into Flnabla0.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Translated differential cells and their closures
items.statement: For w1,w2 in Wplus and s in Wtilde, set Sopen(w1,w2,s)=Sopen_F((w2^-1 w0 w1)^*)s^*. Intersect with Flnabla0, then take its closure inside Flnabla0 to define Snabla0(w1,w2,s). This closure may be strictly smaller than the closure of the entire Schubert cell intersected with Flnabla0.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Dimension of a translated differential cell
items.statement: If w2^-1 w0 w1 is m-small and s is m-generic, with m positive, the differential cell of M20 is affine d-space. Its closure is irreducible of dimension d.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Remove the second dominant factor
items.statement: If wi is mi-small for positive mi, then Sopen(w1,e,s w2^-1)nabla0 embeds closed in Sopen(w1,w2,s)nabla0. If s is(m1+m2)-generic this immersion is equality, and so are their closures. The product is s w2^-1, not w2^-1 s.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Finite Weyl invariance of differential closures
items.statement: For w1 in W1plus and s(n-1)-generic, Snabla0(w1,e,s)=Snabla0(w1,e,s w^-1) for all finite Weyl w. Its proof uses the equality of ambient Schubert closures (Lemma4.3.7) and a rank-one P1 in the differential locus through the adjacent fixed point (Lemma4.3.8); those are separate geometry obligations.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Intrinsic component indexed by an alcove pair
items.statement: For w1 in W1plus and t_omega(n-1)-generic, define C_(w1,omega)=Snabla0(w1,e,s) for any s with s(0)=omega. M23 makes this independent of s; central-equivalent pairs(w1,omega) give the same irreducible d-dimensional closed subvariety.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Identify translated closures intrinsically
items.statement: If w1 in W1plus, w2 in Wplus m-small with m>=1, and s is(m+n-1)-generic, then Snabla0(w1,w2,s)=C_(w1,s w2^-1(0)). The first line of the proof reverses the product once; the statement and Proposition4.3.5 fix the order.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Admissible pairs label translated top components
items.statement: For regular dominant lambda, a in O^n, and s=t_mu sfinite(h_lambda+n-1)-generic with a congruent to sfinite^-1(mu) modulo varpi, AP(lambda) bijects the d-dimensional irreducible components of Mnv(<=lambda,nabla_a)_F s^* by(w1,w2)->C_(w1,s w2^-1(0)).
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Torus torsors over the special-fibre flag
items.statement: Let I1 be loops upper unipotent modulo v. The fpqc quotient I1\LGLn maps to I\LGLn as a Tdual-torsor. Pull it back to each local-model special fibre, to Flnabla0 and to C_(w,omega); the last is irreducible of dimension d+n. No global O-model of these torsors is asserted in §4.4; later constructions only provide torsors on chart covers.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Product models, components and torsor comparison
items.statement: For finite J take products over O (over F for special fibres). Admissible sets are products, d_J=|J|d, and component varieties C_(w,omega) are products of dimension d_J with torus lifts of dimension d_J+n|J|. If z_j=s_j^-1 t_mu_j and a_j congruent s_j^-1(mu_j), translations give a Cartesian square of closed immersions with both vertical maps smooth Tdual^J-torsors.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Component labelled by a Serre weight and central lift
items.statement: For an(n-1)-deep Serre weight sigma and an algebraic central lift zeta, choose its unique zeta-compatible lowest-alcove presentation(w1,omega) and define C_sigma^zeta=C_(w1,omega). This is independent of representatives. The depth condition is part of the definition's domain.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Representation-theoretic component labelling with repaired bound
items.statement: For regular dominant lambda and a Deligne–Lusztig R with a chosen(s,mu) presentation(lambda-eta)-compatible with zeta, assume m-genericity with m>=max(2n,h_lambda+n-1), and a congruent to s^-1(mu+eta) modulo varpi. Then the d_J-dimensional components of Mnv_J(<=lambda,nabla_a)_F(s^-1 t_(mu+eta)) are exactly C_sigma^zeta for sigma in JH(Rbar tensor W(lambda-eta)). The printed bound max(2n,h_lambda) is insufficient for M29's domain and M26's hypothesis; the p19 GL2 test in the reading ledger forces this repair. Preserve it as a source issue, not an unannounced strengthening.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Fixed points detected by the negative-loop chart
items.statement: For finite-type irreducible closed Y in Fl stable under Tdual times loop rotation, fixed point z, and open dense Yopen in Y, z lies in Y iff Y meets L--G z iff Yopen meets L--G z. Use the contracting chart cocharacter and irreducibility.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Obvious fixed points of an intrinsic component
items.statement: For C_(w1,omega), its Tdual^J-fixed points include all(t_omega s w1)^* for finite Weyl tuples s.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Polynomial-generic fixed-point saturation
items.statement: For each restricted affine component w1_j there exists a nonzero integral polynomial P_(w1_j) depending only on it, such that if P_(w1_j)(omega_j) is nonzero modulo p for every j, then the fixed points of C_(w1,omega) are exactly{w^* t_omega:w<=w0 w1}. The proof deforms b v g'g^-1+Ad(g)Diag(a), specializes b=0 to an affine Springer fibre, uses Boixeda Alvarez Theorem3.1, and spreads nonempty chart intersections to b=1. The external fixed-point theorem remains a prerequisite-reading obligation.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Intrinsic component is unibranch at fixed points
items.statement: Each C_(w1,omega) is unibranch at all its Tdual^J-fixed points, by applying the contracting-chart normalization argument to its intersection with the corresponding open chart.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Obvious weight gives a fixed point
items.statement: For sigma(n-1)-deep and rhobar with2(n-1)-generic presentation(s,mu), and their presentations compatible with the same zeta, sigma in Wobv(rhobar) implies wtilde(rhobar)^* lies in C_sigma^zeta.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Fixed point implies a predicted weight
items.statement: Under M35's hypotheses, wtilde(rhobar)^* in C_sigma^zeta implies sigma in W?(rhobar). This implication uses the Bruhat upper bound, without M33's polynomial condition.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Predicted weight gives a fixed point under polynomial genericity
items.statement: Under M35's hypotheses and P_(w1_j)(omega_j) nonzero modulo p in every component, sigma in W?(rhobar) implies wtilde(rhobar)^* in C_sigma^zeta. Keep this additional polynomial condition separate from M35–36's numerical depth.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Tame descent coefficient rings
items.statement: For a fixed1-generic presentation(s,mu) of tau, set r=ord(s0...s_(f-1)), K'/K unramified degree r, f'=fr, e'=p^f'-1, L'=K'((-p)^(1/e')). Gamma'=Gal(L'/K'), Gamma=Gal(L'/K). S_L',R=(W(k') tensor R)[[u']], phi acts by Witt Frobenius, identity on R, u'->u'^p. Gamma' scales u' by the fundamental character; the unramified generator acts on coefficients. v=u'^e', E(v)=v+p, and Gamma invariants give(W(k) tensor R)[[v]]. Retain the J'->J embedding-index projection and sigma_j=sigma0 Frobenius^-j.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Integral Iwahori and its pro-unipotent subgroup
items.statement: I(R) consists of invertible R[[v]] matrices upper triangular modulo v; I1 has unipotent upper triangular reduction. I=Tdual semidirect I1. For p-adically complete Noetherian O-algebras, R[[v+p]]=R[[v]] and I=L+G_O; for p-nilpotent R, the Laurent rings agree. These comparisons do not hold for arbitrary O-algebras, and Frobenius on the shifted series ring requires the stated completeness.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Breuil–Kisin module of bounded height
items.statement: For p-adically complete R, Y^[0,h](R) consists of finite projective rank-n S_L',R modules M with an injective linearized Frobenius phi* M->M whose cokernel is killed by E(v)^h. Embedding decomposition gives partial Frobenius from the j'-1 summand to j'; j' denotes the target embedding.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Tame descent type on Breuil–Kisin modules
items.statement: Y^[0,h],tau adds a semilinear Gamma-action commuting with Frobenius and M^(j')/u' M^(j') isomorphic to tau-dual tensor R as a Gamma'-representation. Extending Gamma' descent is equivalent to an isomorphism for the unramified generator satisfying its cocycle condition. This functor is a p-adic formal algebraic stack, via CEGS and Caraiani–Levin; the dual type is forced by the contravariant Galois functor.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Eigenbasis with descent compatibility
items.statement: An eigenbasis is an ordered basis in each embedding summand with ith vector carrying character chi_i^-1 from(2.12), compatible with the unramified descent isomorphism up to the permutation s_tau. The bases are chosen relative to the fixed presentation of tau.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Oriented partial Frobenius matrices
items.statement: Extend alpha to J' by alpha'_(j+kf)=s_tau^-k(alpha_j), put a'^(j')=sum_(i=0)^(f'-1)p^i alpha'_(-j'+i), and s'_or,j+kf=s_tau^(k+1)s_(f-1)^-1...s_(j+1)^-1. For raw Frobenius matrix C^(j'), define A^(j')=Ad((s'_or,j')^-1 u'^(-a'^(j')))(C^(j')). Orientation makes(s'_or)^-1 a' dominant. A depends only on j' modulo f, lies in L+M, and the height condition is E(v)^h A^-1 in L+M. Spell out this construction rather than identifying it with a change of type.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Compatibility with earlier embedding conventions
items.statement: The earlier LLHL/LLHLM presentation is(s_minus,j,mu_minus,j)=(s_(f-j),mu_(f-j)); its partial Frobenius index is j'-1 for the present target-indexed j'. The orientation, a' exponents and chi characters agree after this translation, and the old star factor becomes s_j+1^-1 t_(mu_j+1+eta_j+1). Use these explicit adapters for all cited earlier lemmas.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Change of eigenbasis is twisted Frobenius conjugation
items.statement: If beta2^(j') D^(j')=beta1^(j'), then I^(j')=Ad((s'_or)^-1 u'^(-a'))D lies in I(R), depends only on j' modulo f, and A_beta2^j=I^j A_beta1^j Ad(s_j^-1 v^(mu_j+eta_j))(phi(I^(j-1)))^-1. Conversely every such periodic tuple in I gives an eigenbasis change.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Shape of a residual Kisin module
items.statement: For M over a field F'/F, its shape relative to the chosen tau presentation is z in Wtilde-dual^J with A_beta^j in I(F') z_j I(F') for every eigenbasis. The change-of-basis formula proves independence of beta.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Frobenius contraction on I1
items.statement: For an m-generic presentation(s,mu) and I in I1(R), Ad(s_j^-1 v^(mu_j+eta_j))(phi(I)) is congruent to1 modulo v^(m+1).
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Higher congruence contraction
items.statement: For m>=1 and k>=1, an invertible I congruent to1 modulo v^k has twisted Frobenius congruent to1 modulo v^((k-1)p+m+1). For a matrix Y divisible by v^k its twisted Frobenius is divisible by the same power. Keep the group and linear variants as separate API lemmas.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Lie I1 Frobenius contraction, corrected
items.statement: The linearization needed subsequently is: if Y modulo v is STRICTLY upper triangular, then Ad(s_j^-1 v^(mu_j+eta_j))(phi(Y)) is divisible by v^(m+1). The printed version only assumes upper triangular and omits phi; Y=identity refutes it. Both repairs are required, and this source issue must be recorded before using the result.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Height-bounded loop spaces
items.statement: For integers a<=b, L^[a,b]G_O requires g in(v+p)^a L+M and(v+p)^b g^-1 in L+M; take its positive-loop quotient Gr^[a,b]. Separately L^[a,b]GLn_F requires v^-a A and v^b A^-1 integral matrices, without Iwahori lower-entry restrictions; its quotient Fl^[a,b] is finite type closed. Gr^[a,b]_F is generally a strict subspace of Fl^[a,b]. Central translation shifts both height bounds.
