items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Twisted conjugation actions
items.statement: On loop tuples, I acts on A by I^j A^j Ad(s_j^-1 v^(mu_j+eta_j))(phi(I^(j-1)))^-1. The twisted conjugation action without Frobenius uses the same formula with phi omitted. Later residual torus actions agree because phi fixes constants; the full mixed-characteristic I1 actions need not agree.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Quotient presentation of the Kisin stack
items.statement: For a lowest-alcove presentation of tau, Y^[0,h],tau is the p-adic completion of the quotient of(L^[0,h]G_O)^J by twisted Frobenius conjugation of(L+G_O)^J. Eigenbases form torsors locally and exist Zariski locally by prime-to-p descent averaging.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Residual straightening of I1 conjugation
items.statement: For an F-algebra R, A1,A2 in L^[0,h]GLn(R)^J and z=s^-1 t_(mu+eta) with mu(h+1)-deep, tuples I in I1^J satisfying A2^j z_j=I^j A1^j z_j phi(I^(j-1))^-1 biject tuples X in I1^J satisfying A2^j=X_j A1^j. The inverse is a v-adic contraction; this is a residual statement.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Residual Kisin stack as a torus quotient
items.statement: If mu is(h+1)-deep, Y^[0,h],tau_F identifies with the quotient of the I1-torsor lift of Gr^[0,h]_F^J by the(s,mu)-twisted Tdual^J conjugation action, and embeds in the analogous bounded flag quotient.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Gauge opens and gauge bases
items.statement: Residual chart covers from U(z) define an open substack Y^[0,h],tau_F(z); its p-adic open thickening is Y^[0,h],tau(z). M admits z-gauge when its reduction lies there. A z-gauge basis is an eigenbasis with every A_beta^j in Tdual(R)U(z_j)(R). Shape z implies z-gauge over a field, but gauge is an open condition whereas fixed shape is only locally closed.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Existence and uniqueness of gauge bases
items.statement: For mu(h+1)-deep, R Noetherian p-adically complete and M admitting an eigenbasis and z-gauge, a z-gauge basis exists and is unique up to Tdual^J(R) scaling (the J'-tuple is constant modulo f). The induction splits Lie LG=Lie L--G direct-sum Lie T direct-sum Lie I1, then inverts identity minus a topologically nilpotent operator. Lie I1 has strictly upper triangular reduction; the proof's printed 'unipotent' is incorrect for a Lie module.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Local model diagram for bounded-height Kisin modules
items.statement: For mu(h+1)-deep and z, the p-completed lifted chart U^[0,h](z) has two Tdual^J-torsor maps: to Y^[0,h],tau(z) by twisted conjugation and to U^[0,h](z) by left translation. Both targets embed openly into the Kisin stack and bounded Grassmannian respectively. The actions are different; the diagrams glue globally over F, but not generally over O (Warning5.3.2).
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Bounded Hodge-type Kisin substack
items.statement: For effective dominant tuple lambda_j in[0,h]^n, Y^<=lambda,tau is the O-flat p-adic formal closed substack with reduced versal rings whose finite-DVR points have Hodge type<=lambda. This is the elementary-divisor condition A_beta^j in the generic Schubert closure SE(lambda_j), established using the graded chi-isotypic pieces of M/E(v)M.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Pappas–Zhu local model diagram with Hodge bound
items.statement: For mu(h+1)-deep, lambda_j in[0,h]^n and z, K20 restricts to the lifted chart U(z,<=lambda), with torsor targets Y^<=lambda,tau(z) and the open chart U(z,<=lambda) of M_J(<=lambda). Take p-adic completions throughout. Equality of the reduced flat pullbacks is checked on finite-extension DVR points.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Nonempty Kisin charts are admissible
items.statement: Under K22's hypotheses, Y^<=lambda,tau(z) is nonempty iff z belongs to Adm-dual(lambda).
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Hodge-bound membership detected by shape
items.statement: Under K22's hypotheses, for finite F'/F a module M over F' lies in Y^<=lambda,tau iff its shape relative to tau is in Adm-dual(lambda).
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Etale Frobenius modules with descent
items.statement: O_E,K is the p-adic completion of W(k)[[v]][1/v], and O_E,L' the analogous u' ring. Rank-n finite projective modules over their completed tensor product with R carry semilinear Frobenius whose linearization is an isomorphism, with commuting Gamma descent in the L' version. They form fppf stacks over Spf O.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Forget the Kisin lattice and descend
items.statement: epsilon_tau(M) is the Gamma-invariant part after inverting u' and completing. It defines a map from Y^[0,h],tau to the etale Frobenius stack independent of the chosen presentation. Descent invariants give an equivalence between the etale module stack with L'/K descent and the K-valued one, inverse to scalar extension.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Properness of the lattice-forgetting map
items.statement: epsilon_tau is representable by algebraic spaces, proper and of finite presentation, using CEGS's bounded-height lattice moduli and descent equivalence.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Etale Frobenius matrix attached to an eigenbasis
items.statement: An eigenbasis beta determines a basis of epsilon_tau(M) in which the jth partial Frobenius matrix is A_beta^j s_j^-1 v^(mu_j+eta_j). This is the explicit compatibility with K08 and is needed to compare different types inside one etale stack.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Generic triviality of Kisin fibres as a closed immersion
items.statement: For h>=0 and tau(h+1)-generic, epsilon_tau is a monomorphism of p-adic formal stacks and hence a closed immersion. This is full faithfulness on all allowed coefficient rings, stronger than uniqueness only at field-valued points.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Pole elimination for etale isomorphisms
items.statement: For R an F-algebra, A1,A2 in L^[0,h]GLn(R)^J and z=s^-1 t_(mu+eta) with mu(h+1)-deep, any tuple I in GLn(R((v)))^J with A2^j z_j=I^j A1^j z_j phi(I^(j-1))^-1 actually lies in I_F(R)^J. The cyclic pole-order inequalities first eliminate negative powers, then force upper-triangular reduction.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Pole elimination for infinitesimal isomorphisms
items.statement: Under the same depth/height hypotheses, for an R-module J and Y_j in Matn(J((v))) with Y_j-Ad(A^j z_j)phi(Y_(j-1)) in v^-h Matn(J[[v]]), all Y_j lie in Lie I_F(J). This lifts K30 across coefficient nilpotents.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Translated bounded flags and shifted torus action
items.statement: Fl^[a,b]_(J,z) is the product of I1\\(L^[a,b]GLn)z_j. For z=sigma^-1 t_(nu+eta) and nu(b-a+1)-deep, the Frobenius-matrix map descends to this flag lift and then to the shifted Tdual^J conjugation quotient, where D acts by D_j A_j z_j D_(j-1)^-1.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Bounded flag quotient embeds in the etale stack
items.statement: Under K32's depth hypothesis, iota_z from the shifted-torus quotient of Fl^[a,b]_(J,z) to the etale Frobenius stack over F is a monomorphism.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Compatibility diagram for different local models
items.statement: Assume a<=b,h>=0; z=sigma^-1 t_(nu+eta) with nu(b-a+1)-deep; tau has(h+1)-deep presentation(s,mu); the translated bounded Gr^[0,h]^J by w*(tau) lies in Fl^[a,b]_(J,z); and lambda_j in[0,h]^n. Then the PZ special-fibre torsor, the Kisin stacks, right translation by w*(tau), the torus quotient and epsilon_tau commute in diagram(5.13). The inclusion is an explicit hypothesis when comparing multiple types.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Fields-of-norms anti-equivalence
items.statement: For R complete Noetherian local over O with finite residue field, etale Frobenius modules over K are exactly anti-equivalent to rank-n continuous R-representations of GK_infinity by the dual of Frobenius-fixed vectors after unramified period extension. Tdd*=V_K* composed with epsilon_tau. The paper explicitly corrects the formula in[59] §2.3; this already-known correction needs a sourceIssues entry with that attribution.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Restriction of tame representations and semisimplification
items.statement: GK_infinity surjects onto the tame quotient of GK, hence restriction is fully faithful on tame representations and tame GK_infinity representations extend canonically. Semisimple finite-characteristic representations are tame. The converse printed identification of tameness with semisimplicity is false without further regular-inertia hypotheses: an unramified nontrivial2x2 unipotent Frobenius representation is tame and nonsplit.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Genericity of a residual Galois representation
items.statement: rho is m-generic if the tame inertial type of rho^ss is m-generic. For tame rho a lowest-alcove presentation means a presentation of its inertial restriction, giving w(rho)=t_(mu+eta)s and w*(rho)=s^-1t_(mu+eta). This definition must not silently discard a nonsemisimple unramified extension.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Semisimple representations from torus-fixed Frobenius matrices
items.statement: For a fixed point z' in the bounded translated flag of Proposition5.4.7 and semisimple rho, rho has a presentation with w*(rho)=z' iff for some D in Tdual^J(F), V_K*(iota_z(Dz')) is rho restricted to GK_infinity. Torus constants account for the unramified extension of the prescribed inertial parameter.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Shape of a residual representation relative to a type
items.statement: If rho|GK_infinity has a Kisin lift M in Y^[0,h],tau(F), define its shape relative to tau to be the shape of M. The generic closed-immersion theorem makes it independent of M; it is undefined if no such lift exists.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Semisimple Kisin module
items.statement: M is semisimple of shape z when in the z-gauge diagram its image in the ordinary chart is the torus-fixed point z. Equivalently it has an eigenbasis with A_beta^j in Tdual(F') z_j in every component.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Semisimple Kisin modules and admissible type position
items.statement: For tau(h+1)-generic and semisimple rho of GK_infinity, a semisimple M in Y^[0,h],tau with Tdd*(M)=rho exists iff rho admits a presentation with z=w*(rho)w*(tau)^-1 in Gr^[0,h]^J_F. Its shape is z. Furthermore M belongs to Y^<=lambda,tau iff w(tau)^-1 w(rho) belongs to Adm(lambda).
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: A nonzero tame deformation ring forces admissibility
items.statement: For tame rho, effective lambda_j in[0,h]^n and tau as in K41, a nonzero R_rho^(lambda,tau) implies a lambda-compatible presentation of rho with w(tau)^-1 w(rho) in Adm(lambda). Check that the genericity used forces the semisimple case needed in the proof; do not invoke the false unqualified tame=semisimple assertion.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Semisimplification preserves a Kisin height and Hodge bound
items.statement: For finite F'/F and M in Y^<=lambda,tau(F') (or Y^[0,h],tau(F')), there is a semisimple M' in the same substack with Tdd*(M')=Tdd*(M)^ss. Use a descent-compatible filtration, a cocharacter degeneration over A1 and properness of the lattice map. Density is that of Gm as a subscheme, not the finite set F'^times.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Residual genericity loses at most the height
items.statement: For finite F'/F, M in Y^[0,h],tau(F') and tau m-generic with m>=h+1, Tdd*(M)^ss has an(m-h)-generic lowest-alcove presentation. Reduce to K43, then bound the translation difference by the height.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Framed local lifting ring
items.statement: For a continuous rho:GL->G(F), with L a characteristic-zero nonarchimedean local field and G a split possibly disconnected reductive O-group, liftings to Noetherian complete local O-algebras with residue F form the framed lifting functor represented by R_rho^square. Retain the group/ring hypotheses and do not quotient by conjugacy.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Type and Hodge-type deformation quotients
items.statement: For GLn and L away from p, R_rho^tau is the reduced O-flat quotient with the prescribed inertial type. For L above p and dominant Hodge lambda and WD inertial tau, R_rho^(lambda,tau) is the reduced O-flat Zariski closure of characteristic-zero potentially semistable points of that exact type; R_rho^(lambda,<=tau) is the reduced union over monodromy types dominated by tau. If N_tau=0 this is the potentially crystalline ring and a versal ring of X^(lambda,tau); a maximal tau gives the usual semistable union.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Patched local base rings
items.statement: For finitely many unramified p-adic places, take the completed tensor product R_rho of framed local lifting rings and R_infinity=R_rho completed-tensor R^p, where R^p is nonzero complete Noetherian local, equidimensional and O-flat with residue F. Define R_infinity(lambda,tau) using the Hodge type lambda+eta. The representation sigma(lambda,tau)=V(lambda) tensor sigma(tau) uses lambda, so preserve this shift.
items.note: Route owner: DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Weak patching functor
items.statement: A weak patching functor is a nonzero covariant exact functor from finite O-module continuous GLn(Op)-representations to coherent R_infinity-modules, taking every stable lattice sigma^circ(lambda,tau) to a maximal Cohen–Macaulay module on X_infinity(lambda,<=tau), and every residual constituent to a maximal Cohen–Macaulay module there or zero. The support includes the monodromy-dominated union.
items.note: Route owner: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIPatchedGLdDensity. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Weak minimal patching functor
items.statement: A weak functor is minimal if R^p is formally smooth over O and, for each zero-monodromy inertial tau, the generic-fibre module of every type lattice is locally free of rank at most one on each connected component of the regular generic deformation fibre.
items.note: Route owner: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIPatchedGLdDensity. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Potentially diagonalizable patching functor
items.statement: A weak functor is potentially diagonalizable when it is nonzero on a type lattice whenever each residual local representation has a potentially diagonalizable lift of the corresponding Hodge type lambda_v+eta_v and inertial type tau_v.
items.note: Route owner: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIPatchedGLdDensity. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Detectable patching functor
items.statement: For semisimple2n-generic rho, a weak functor is detectable when it is nonzero on every obvious Serre weight of rho.
items.note: Route owner: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIPatchedGLdDensity. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Minimal patching functor for a set of types
items.statement: For a set S of pairs(lambda+eta,tau) with N_tau=0, a minimal patching functor is a weak minimal one whose generic-fibre module has rank exactly one over the entire Spec R_infinity(lambda,tau)[1/p] for every pair in S and every type lattice. Rank at most one does not imply this full-support property.
items.note: Route owner: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIPatchedGLdDensity. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Weight elimination for weak patching functors
items.statement: If M_infinity(sigma) is nonzero, then sigma belongs to W?(rho^ss) provided either every local rho_v^ss is(6n-2)-generic, or sigma is(2n-1)-deep and every rho_v^ss is4n-generic. The two alternatives are separate sufficient hypotheses.
items.note: Route owner: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIPatchedGLdDensity. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Existence of potentially diagonalizable weak patching
items.statement: If p does not divide2n, every residual L-homomorphism in the section's unramified setup has a weak potentially diagonalizable patching functor. This is a global construction using globalization, potentially diagonalizable lifts and Taylor–Wiles patching, not a formal existence axiom.
items.note: Route owner: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIPatchedGLdDensity. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Existence of weak minimal potentially diagonalizable patching
items.statement: Under P10, if each rho_v has a potentially diagonalizable lift of a type for which the product potentially crystalline lifting ring is formally smooth, then a weak minimal potentially diagonalizable functor exists.
items.note: Route owner: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIPatchedGLdDensity. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Detectability for semisimple generic representations
items.statement: For K/Qp finite unramified, p not dividing2n, and semisimple rho with4n-generic inertia, every weak potentially diagonalizable functor is detectable, and a weak minimal detectable potentially diagonalizable functor exists. Fontaine–Laffaille formally smooth lift existence supplies P11's hypothesis.
items.note: Route owner: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIPatchedGLdDensity. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Patched nonvanishing and admissibility criterion
items.statement: For semisimple rho with4n-generic inertia, dominant effective lambda_j in[0,h]^n, tau with chosen max(2n,h+n-1)-generic presentation, a stable lattice sigma^circ(lambda,tau), and a weak detectable minimal functor, the following are equivalent: its patched module is nonzero; R_infinity(lambda,tau) is nonzero; R_rho^(lambda+eta,tau) is nonzero; rho admits a lambda-compatible presentation with w(tau)^-1 w(rho) in Adm(lambda+eta). Expand the equivalence into individual implications in the blueprint. No domain claim is involved.
items.note: Route owner: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIPatchedGLdDensity. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Ordinary upper-triangular lifting
items.statement: Let kappa in X1 be(n-1)-deep and rho upper triangular with diagonal characters chi_bar_i having inertia product_j baromega_(K,sigma_j)^(kappa_j,i+eta_j,i). It admits an upper triangular lift with inertia characters chi_i=epsilon^(n-i) product_j omega_(K,sigma_j)^kappa_j,i. Every such lift is potentially crystalline of type(eta,tau(1,kappa)). The proof uses local H2 obstruction vanishing, de Rham extension results, and distinct inertial characters to kill monodromy.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Ordinary weights detected by potentially diagonalizable patching
items.statement: For kappa,rho as in P14, assume rho4n-generic. Every weak potentially diagonalizable functor has M_infinity(F(kappa)) nonzero. Weight elimination and the singleton obvious-weight intersection isolate F(kappa) from the type lattice.
items.note: Route owner: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIPatchedGLdDensity. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Ordinary constituent forces a nonzero lifting ring
items.statement: Under P15's hypotheses, if F(kappa) is a constituent of the reduction of sigma(lambda,tau), then R_rho^(lambda+eta,tau) is nonzero.
items.note: Route owner: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIPatchedGLdDensity. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Rigid coefficient rings and analytic derivation
items.statement: For a p-adically complete topologically finite type O-flat algebra R, define O^rig_R as the inverse limit of R[[u',u'^m/p]][1/p], with its convergent analytic interpretation. Define the analytic product L=product_{i>=0} phi^i(E(u')/p) and N_nabla=-u'L d/du'. Evaluation at roots of phi^i(E) is available in this analytic ring; it is not an operation on arbitrary R[1/p][[u']].
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Kisin monodromy operator on a lattice
items.statement: For M over a finite flat O-algebra of height [0,h] with tame descent, there is a unique derivation extending N_nabla on M^rig[1/L], zero modulo u' and satisfying N phi=E phi N. The lattice M^rig is stable precisely when T_dd^*(M)[1/p] extends to a potentially crystalline GK representation of type tau and Hodge–Tate weights in [0,h]. This imports Kisin [48].
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: True monodromy condition
items.statement: A Breuil–Kisin module satisfies monodromy when its rigid lattice is preserved by the unique operator of G02. Keep this condition distinct from the finite truncated equations of G10.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Family monodromy recurrence
items.statement: For an O-flat complete topologically finite type R and an eigenbasis with Frobenius matrices C_j, set N_0,j=0 and N_i,j=E C_j phi(N_{i-1,j-1}) C_j^-1-N_nabla(C_j) C_j^-1. Its coefficientwise limit is the unique family monodromy operator, lies in L^(1-h) Mat(O^rig_R), and satisfies the explicit denominator/convergence estimate (7.4). Cyclic embedding indices are essential.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Finite derivative criterion for monodromy
items.statement: Over finite flat O coefficients, monodromy holds iff all derivatives of L^(h-1)N_infty at E=0 of orders 0 through h-2 vanish for every embedding. Frobenius compatibility propagates the criterion to the other zeros of L. The h=1 range is empty.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Closed generic monodromy locus
items.statement: When M is free over the allowed R, the criterion defines a basis-independent Zariski closed locus in Spec R[1/p], compatible with base change among these pairs.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Integral true monodromy ideal
items.statement: There is a unique ideal I_{M,nabla infinity} with O-flat quotient obtained by closing the generic monodromy locus after flat local trivializations. It commutes with flat base change; arbitrary base change only gives I_M S contained in I_{M_S}. Do not replace that inclusion by equality.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Monodromy leading term and error series
items.statement: Removing tame descent from p^h L^(h-1)N_infty gives -phi(L)^h P_N(A_j) plus the convergent sum phi^(i+1)(L)^h Z_i,j. Define P_N(A)=(-e' v A' -[Diag(s_or^-1 a'),A])(v+p)^h A^-1 and the iterated Frobenius error terms Z_i. Preserve their v-adic and p-denominator estimates, used to obtain the integral precision bound G11.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Truncated monodromy ideal
items.statement: Given an eigenbasis beta, I_{M,beta,nabla1} is generated by derivatives of v^(-[k>l])P_N(A_j)_{kl} at v=-p, of orders 0 through h-2, for every j,k,l. This ideal is basis dependent as presented and is not the true ideal by definition.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Truncated differential local-model equation
items.statement: If p>h-2, vanishing of the derivatives is equivalent to divisibility by (v+p)^(h-1), and hence to (e'v A'-A Diag(s_or^-1 a'))A^-1 in (v+p)^-1 L^+M. The corresponding local-model parameter is -(s_or^-1 a')/e'.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Integral precision of the leading monodromy equations
items.statement: For an m-deep lowest-alcove presentation and a height [0,h] module over allowed O-flat complete R with eigenbasis, I_nabla1 is contained in (I_nabla infinity,p^(m-2h+3)). Use m>=2h-3 for an integral ideal statement, as explicitly imposed in the subsequent application. The theorem gives containment, not equality of ideals.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Emerton–Gee representation stack
items.statement: Import the Noetherian formal algebraic stack X_n of projective rank n étale (phi,Gamma)-modules from [22]. On complete local Noetherian O-algebras with finite residue field it represents the groupoid of continuous rank n GK representations. For a finite étale Z_p-algebra take products over its field factors.
items.note: Route owner: WeightZeroCrystallineLiftingRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Potentially crystalline formal substacks
items.statement: X^{lambda,tau} is the unique O-flat closed formal substack characterized on finite flat O-algebras by potentially crystalline type (lambda,tau). Define X^{[0,h],tau} and X^{<=lambda,tau} as scheme-theoretic unions over the indicated dominant weights, not as reduced unions.
items.note: Route owner: WeightZeroCrystallineLiftingRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Analytically unramified formal stack
items.statement: A topologically finite type p-adic formal algebraic stack is analytically unramified when all smooth affine charts have reduced rings, equivalently its finite-type versal rings are reduced. Its associated reduced formal stack pulls back to Spf A_red. Distinguish this from the underlying reduced algebraic stack Spec(A/I)_red.
items.note: Route owner: SchemeAndStackFoundations. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Geometry and versal rings of crystalline stacks
items.statement: For ?=[0,h], <=lambda, or lambda, X^{?,tau} is O-flat, analytically unramified and topologically finite type; smooth chart generic fibers are regular; at a residual point the corresponding potentially crystalline deformation ring is a versal ring. Imports [22], [28], [49]; the proof cites [23] three times where the input is [22], corrected in E32.
items.note: Route owner: WeightZeroCrystallineLiftingRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Dimension of a crystalline stack
items.statement: X^{lambda,tau} is equidimensional of dimension 1+sum_j dim(P_{lambda_j}\GL_n), with the Hodge convention that epsilon has weight +1. Translation to [22] replaces lambda by -w0(lambda).
items.note: Route owner: WeightZeroCrystallineLiftingRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Fiber products and monodromy substacks
items.statement: Define K^{?,tau}=X^{?,tau} fiber product over étale phi modules with Y^{?,tau}. Define Y^{[0,h],tau,nabla infinity} and Y^{<=lambda,tau,nabla infinity} by the flat-closed ideal G07. These are stacks on complete coefficient rings, not merely sets of characteristic-zero points.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Kisin/crystalline stack comparison
items.statement: For h>=1, an (h+2)-generic tau and dominant lambda_j in [0,h]^n, the diagram (7.11) identifies X^{[0,h],tau} with Y^{[0,h],tau,nabla infinity} and X^{<=lambda,tau} with Y^{<=lambda,tau,nabla infinity}. Its specified rectangles and trapezoids are Cartesian, except that the top-right rectangle is not asserted Cartesian. The rightmost lower arrow is only a monomorphism, the other hooked arrows are closed immersions.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Artinian points detect scheme isomorphisms
items.statement: A map of finite type O/varpi^a schemes inducing a bijection on A-points for every local Artinian A with finite residue field is an isomorphism. The proof uses infinitesimal smoothness, quasi-finiteness, and the étale monomorphism criterion.
items.note: Route owner: SchemeAndStackFoundations. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Finite-flat points detect formal-stack isomorphisms
items.statement: For a monomorphism Y->Z of topologically finite type p-adic formal algebraic stacks with Z O-flat, an isomorphism follows from each of: Z analytically unramified plus essential surjectivity on all finite-flat O-algebras; a closed immersion with Z analytically unramified plus surjectivity on all finite extension rings of integers; or a closed immersion plus surjectivity on all finite-flat O-algebras. These are three separate sufficient criteria.
items.note: Route owner: SchemeAndStackFoundations. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Existence and uniqueness of Kisin lattices in families
items.statement: If tau is (h+1)-generic then K^{[0,h],tau}->X^{[0,h],tau} is an isomorphism. Consequently the unique lattice attached to a representation over any finite-flat O-algebra is projective over the corresponding Breuil–Kisin coefficient ring, not only projective after forgetting that algebra action.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Cyclotomic-free residual representation
items.statement: A residual representation is cyclotomic free when a prime-to-p unramified extension M/K makes its semisimplification a sum of characters and H^0(G_M,rho_ss tensor epsilon^-1)=0.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Restriction full faithfulness under cyclotomic freeness
items.statement: Cyclotomic-free rho has H^0(GK,rho)=H^0(GK_infty,rho). Two-generic inertia implies ad(rho) cyclotomic free. If finite-length O[GK]-modules V,W have semisimplifications in finite sums of a fixed residual rho with cyclotomic-free adjoint, restriction is an isomorphism on Hom; every GK_infty-submodule of W is GK-stable.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Restriction monomorphism for crystalline families
items.statement: If tau is (h+2)-generic, X^{[0,h],tau}->X_n->étale phi modules is a monomorphism on groupoids over the full coefficient category, proved first on finite Artinian rings and then by represented isomorphism functors.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Monodromy produces the integral Galois representation
items.statement: Under the standing (h+2)-generic hypotheses, K^{[0,h],tau} and K^{<=lambda,tau} map isomorphically onto the respective true-monodromy substacks. The integral step says that for M over finite-flat O coefficients, if T_dd^*(M)[1/p] extends to GK, its original GK_infty lattice is GK-stable.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Presentation-dependent local-model parameter
items.statement: Set a_{tau,j'}=(s_or,j')^-1(a'^(j'))/(1-p^f'). It depends on the chosen lowest-alcove presentation, and reduces to s_j^-1(mu_j+eta_j) modulo varpi for j in J.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Regular-weight unions and framed charts
items.statement: Define M_{J,reg}(<=lambda,nabla a_tau) as the scheme-theoretic union of the flat models for regular dominant lambda'<=lambda. It is the maximal O-flat closed part equidimensional of dimension 1+|J|n(n-1)/2. Define the corresponding affine charts, torus torsors, regular crystalline union X_reg, and formal pullbacks in (7.13).
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Approximate equations give a noncanonical closed immersion
items.statement: For regular dominant lambda_j in [0,h]^n and an (h+2)-lowest-alcove presentation of tau, there is N_sing depending only on the set of lambda_j, not p, such that N_sing-depth supplies the diagonal closed immersion from the true-monodromy formal chart to the naive differential formal chart. It lifts the mod-p map using Elkik approximation and is not canonical or required to commute with the ambient triangle.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Polynomial-generic regular local-model isomorphism
items.statement: There is a nonzero integral polynomial P depending only on {lambda_j} and the ramification index e of O, not p, such that P-genericity of the presentation makes the vertical map between the framed X_reg chart and the p-completed regular differential chart an isomorphism. All marked solid pullback squares and torus torsors are part of the construction; the isomorphism is not a global canonical gluing over O.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Domain versal rings at semisimple points
items.statement: Under G29, for every regular dominant lambda'<=lambda and every semisimple residual GK representation rho, every corresponding versal ring of X^{lambda',tau} is a domain or zero. No assertion for arbitrary wild residual representations. Products over finitely many unramified local fields retain the theorem by Remark7.3.4.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Nonempty crystalline shape charts
items.statement: For regular lambda'_j in [0,h']^n and a (4n+h')-generic lowest-alcove presentation, X^{lambda',tau}(z) is nonempty iff z lies in Adm^vee(lambda'). The nonempty direction imports potentially diagonalizable obvious-weight lifts and the detectability criterion, not just existence of a Kisin lattice.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Serre-labelled Emerton–Gee components
items.statement: Import the irreducible-component labelling of X_n,red from [22, Theorem6.5.1]. The paper defines C_sigma using the dual/det^(n-1) relabelling. For 1-deep sigma=F(kappa), a dense locus consists of maximally nonsplit upper triangular representations with diagonal inertia characters product_j omega_j^((kappa_j+eta_j)_i). Retain the tres-ramifiee boundary rule for nondeep weights.
items.note: Route owner: WeightZeroCrystallineLiftingRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Special-fiber factorization through the naive local model
items.statement: Under the standing (h+2)-generic setup and the additional (2h-2)-depth bound, the framed X^{<=lambda,tau}_F closed immersion in M_J(<=lambda)_F factors through M_J^naive(<=lambda,nabla a_tau)_F.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Generic crystalline component support
items.statement: For regular lambda_j in [0,h]^n and a max{2(h+1),4n+h}-deep presentation compatible with lambda-eta and zeta, the reduced X_reg^{<=lambda,tau} and X^{lambda,tau} are the union of C_sigma for sigma in JH(W(lambda-eta) tensor barsigma(tau)). Equidimensionality of the naive model also gives the same reduced union for X^{<=lambda,tau}. Products over unramified field factors are allowed.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Component local-model diagram
items.statement: Under G34, each labelled component pulls back under the T^vee,J torsor to the translate C_sigma^zeta w*(tau)^-1 inside the affine flag space; its quotient description in étale phi modules depends only on zeta. Thus C_sigma is equisingular to a component of the deformed affine Springer fiber. Under the weaker 2(h+1)-depth hypothesis only the stated upper inclusion follows without weight existence.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Dense triangular locus in Springer components
items.statement: For an (n-1)-deep weight with compatible lowest-alcove presentation, the component C_sigma^zeta has an explicitly chosen dense affine open whose associated étale phi modules carry a full flag with diagonal inertia characters determined by kappa+eta. Cyclotomic-free full faithfulness then identifies this flag with the GK flag and fixes the component label.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Component membership and predicted weights
items.statement: For sigma (3n-1)-deep and a tame 2n-generic rho: obvious membership implies rho in C_sigma; predicted membership plus nonvanishing of every polynomial P_{w1,j}(omega_j) implies rho in C_sigma; and rho in C_sigma implies predicted membership. The converse without polynomial genericity is not proved here. Realizing C_sigma in a suitable 2n-generic X^{eta,tau} is part of the argument.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Global top-dimensional stack cycles
items.statement: Define Z[X_n,red] as the free abelian group on Serre-labelled irreducible components C_sigma, with coefficientwise effectivity and order. Define the finite-group representation Grothendieck group and lattice-independent reduction of characteristic-zero representations.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Extremal types and crystalline/semistable cycles
items.statement: A type is (lambda+eta,tau) with lambda dominant and tau a Weil–Deligne inertial type; it is extremal if tau is minimal or maximal for the monodromy order. Its cycle Z_{lambda,tau} records generic-point lengths of X_F^{lambda+eta,tau}. For a set S of types define JH(sigma(S)) as the union of type constituents.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Geometric Breuil–Mézard conjectural interface
items.statement: For a specified set S of extremal types, conjecture effective cycles Z_sigma with Z_{lambda,tau}=sum_sigma [sigma(lambda,tau):sigma]Z_sigma. This is a conjecture in general, not a theorem of the paper; subsequent results prove restricted generic instances. The extra inequality Z_sigma>=C_sigma is likewise conjectural in Remark8.1.2 outside the proved range.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Breuil–Mézard system
items.statement: A set S of extremal types is a Breuil–Mézard system if the map from Z[S] to the representation Grothendieck group has finite cokernel. Such a spanning condition gives uniqueness of cycles if they exist; an arbitrary set S does not give uniqueness.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Versal cycle pullback
items.statement: Given a versal ring R^ver_rho of X_n, form the crystalline quotient and the effective algebraic versal ring R^alg_rho of X_n,red. The effective map i_rho:Spec R^alg_rho->X_n,red induces pullback of component cycles; formal fibers preserve their multiplicities. Record the dependence on the chosen versal ring.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Versal Breuil–Mézard conjectural interface
items.statement: Conjecture effective cycles Z_sigma(rho) satisfying all equations for S on a chosen versal ring. A common formally smooth cover transports the assertion to another versal ring. This general conjecture is not marked proved.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Cycle of a finite module
items.statement: For a finite module on a type's special-fiber versal ring, its top-dimensional cycle sums each irreducible component with coefficient equal to the length of the module localized at its generic prime.
items.note: Route owner: SchemeAndStackFoundations. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Geometric equations imply versal equations
items.statement: Geometric Breuil–Mézard for S implies the versal form at every residual point, by pullback preserving multiplicities.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Component-meeting testing set
items.statement: For P contained in residual stack points, define i_P^* as the product of versal pullbacks. P meets all components of S if every component supporting some type in S contains a point of P.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Cycle detection by versal pullbacks
items.statement: If P meets all components of S, i_P^* is injective on their integral span and detects effectivity. This does not by itself construct global cycles from arbitrary locally chosen cycles.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Descent and uniqueness of candidate cycles
items.statement: Assume P meets every component and versal equations hold at P. For each sigma there is at most one global cycle with the specified support and all chosen local pullbacks; if all exist, they are effective and satisfy geometric equations. Choosing one smooth point on each component supplies existence and proves the converse to B08 in that setting.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Irrelevant weights
items.statement: A weight is (rho,S_elim)-irrelevant if it occurs in a type whose ordered semistable deformation ring is zero; it is (P,S_elim)-irrelevant if this holds for each rho in P. Weak patching vanishes on such weights. If versal BM holds, their cycles vanish as well.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Covering, disjointness and relative genericity for type sets
items.statement: For S, sigma S-covers kappa when every type in S containing sigma has C_kappa in its special-fiber support. Define S-disjointness from S' by excluding every such component from all S' supports. For S contained in S_tilde, relative genericity means S_tilde-disjointness from S_tilde minus S.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Relative Breuil–Mézard system and good subsystem
items.statement: S_tilde is a (P,S_elim)-BM system if every Serre class has a nonzero integer multiple that is an integral combination of its type classes modulo irrelevant weights. Define S_P by requiring all constituents to be relatively generic. This quotient-spanning definition differs from B04.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Minimal patching gives versal cycles
items.statement: If every x in P has a minimal patching functor for S, then the versal equations hold with Z_sigma(x)=Z(M_infty^x(sigma)). The rank-one generic support condition is used for equality with the ring cycle.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Truncated inversion gives effective geometric cycles
items.statement: In addition to B15, assume P meets every S component and S_tilde containing S is a relative P-BM system. Every relatively generic sigma has a unique effective global cycle with the required support and local pullbacks, giving geometric BM for S_P. Construction first inverts the type matrix rationally and then truncates components; versal detection proves integrality and effectivity.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Patching independence and comparison to conjectural cycles
items.statement: Under B16 the cycles are independent of the minimal patching functors, though local cycles still depend on the versal ring. If a larger genuine BM system S_elim containing S_tilde satisfies geometric BM and supplies the relative irrelevant relations, these cycles equal its conjectural cycles.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Component truncation idempotents
items.statement: Define tr_{sigma,S} by retaining exactly the covered components, and its compatible versal version. It kills cycles of excluded types and fixes the patching cycle of sigma. These facts allow rational inversion without introducing undesired components.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Generic crystalline type systems
items.statement: For a finite dominant-weight set Lambda containing zero, define S_{Lambda,t} using subordinate dominant weights and tame types with both P_{lambda+eta,e}-genericity and (6n-2+h_{lambda+eta})-depth. Define P_ss, S_tilde by adjoining 2n-generic weight-zero types, and S_tilde_elim by adjoining all extremal tame-inertia weight-zero types. Keep these three type systems distinct.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Weight elimination makes the enlarged system span
items.statement: For residual tame (6n-2)-generic inertia, weights outside W? are irrelevant for S_tilde_elim. Ordinary character reduction and Deligne–Lusztig constituents then prove that S_tilde is a (P_ss,S_tilde_elim)-BM system.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Abstract covering reduces to combinatorial covering
items.statement: If sigma is (3n-1)-deep and S_tilde-covers kappa, then sigma covers kappa in the finite-group sense of Definition2.3.10. This requires component upper bounds and the genericity comparison, not an identification of the two definitions in all ranges.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Generic Serre weights for BM
items.statement: A weight is generic when it occurs in S_{0,t} and covers no constituent of any type in S_tilde_{0,t} outside S_{0,t}. It is consequently (6n-2)-deep, and every weight it covers is again generic.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Generic weights and semisimple points meet the axioms
items.statement: Generic weights are relatively generic for every S_{Lambda,t}. P_ss meets all components of that system; tame residual points of its crystalline stacks have (6n-2)-generic inertia. The proof constructs obvious semisimple points explicitly.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Minimal patching for tame generic residual representations
items.statement: For semisimple (6n-2)-generic rho there exists a minimal patching functor for S_{Lambda,t}, and its module cycles satisfy the versal BM equations. The domain theorem and detectability upgrade generic rank at most one to rank exactly one.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Generic geometric BM cycles and support
items.statement: For each generic sigma there is a unique cycle with support among C_kappa covered by sigma and pullbacks equal to all chosen minimal patching cycles at P_ss. These cycles are effective by the preceding abstract theorem.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Canonicity of generic BM cycles
items.statement: Generic cycles are independent of the patching choices; local cycles depend only on the versal ring. If full geometric BM holds for a genuine BM system containing S_tilde_elim, its cycles agree with these generic cycles.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Shifted polynomial genericity
items.statement: For an integral polynomial f and dominant omega, define f^omega as the finite product over lattice points nu in Conv(omega) of f(X-nu). Build P_{P,Lambda,e} from the shifted product of P_{eta,e}P_{7n-3}; distinguish this polynomial from the original local-model P_{lambda,e}.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Polynomial-generic geometric BM
items.statement: For finite Lambda containing zero, P_{P,Lambda,e}-generic inertia parameters place all corresponding types in the good subsystem. Effective cycles then solve geometric BM simultaneously for all lambda in Lambda and all such tame types. Cycles outside the occurring generic weights can be assigned zero; uniqueness is only the separately stated generic/very-generic result.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Product compatibility of BM cycles
items.statement: For a finite product of unramified local fields, completed tensor products of patching functors and uniqueness give the corresponding product structure of the generic cycles.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Admissibility transports polynomial genericity
items.statement: For finite dominant Lambda and residual inertia with shifted P_{P,Lambda,e}^eta-generic parameter, any tame tau with relative shape in Adm(lambda+eta) for some lambda in Lambda belongs to the good type subsystem.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Generic small-weight versal BM for all tame WD types
items.statement: For finite dominant Lambda containing zero, let h=max_{lambda in Lambda,alpha} <lambda,alpha^vee> and m=max{2h+2h_eta,6n-2}. If rho_ss inertia has parameters generic for P_{P,Lambda,e}^eta P_m, cycles on the chosen algebraic versal ring satisfy Z(R^{lambda+eta,tau}_{rho,F})=sum_sigma [r(tau) tensor V(lambda):sigma]Z_sigma(rho) for every lambda in Lambda and every tame Weil–Deligne type. The virtual type r(tau) may have signed coefficients. Genuine noncrystalline semistable types have zero relevant rings in this range; this is not a geometric domain theorem for wild rho.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Unit leading coefficient of a generic BM cycle
items.statement: For generic sigma, the coefficient of C_sigma in Z_sigma is one. The argument uses a specially chosen obvious semisimple point where the crystalline deformation ring is formally smooth and a detectable minimal patching functor is nonzero.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Generic BM cycles form an integral basis
items.statement: The generic Z_sigma form a basis of the integral span of the generic C_sigma, via the covering partial order and a unipotent triangular transition matrix.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Defect of a predicted weight
items.statement: For 2n-generic tame residual inertia, the pair (w,w1) indexing sigma in W? defines delta_rho(sigma)=length(t_eta)-length((w_h w)^-1 w0 w1). It is independent of the lowest-alcove presentation, nonnegative, and zero exactly on obvious weights.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Unique maximal defect in a type intersection
items.statement: For compatible 2n-generic tame rho,tau with relative shape in Adm_reg(eta), the factorization w2^-1 w0 w1 determines a unique constituent in W?(rho) intersect JH(barsigma(tau)) maximizing defect.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Recursive BM coefficient computation
items.statement: Choose a type for each predicted sigma so that every other constituent in its predicted intersection has smaller defect. Compute the sigma cycle from the type cycle by subtracting the lower-defect terms and dividing by its positive multiplicity. The displayed (8.3) must exclude kappa=sigma from the sum; the image verifies the omission, recorded in E21. Component-meeting semisimple test points recover global coefficients.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Very-generic uniqueness from polynomial-type equations
items.statement: Two effective solutions to the specified polynomial-generic type equations coincide at sigma0 provided every two-step type intersection through any weight covered by sigma0 remains polynomial generic. Equality holds on all semisimple versal pullbacks and globally. A further polynomial Q guarantees this stronger condition; arbitrary finite Lambda alone does not.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Definite unitary global setting
items.statement: Fix a CM extension F/F+ with F+ totally real and not Q, all p-adic places split in F, and a form of GL_n over F+ split over F and definite at infinity. Choose its integral model away from N prime to p, a place above each split place, and identifications with GL_n locally. Assume F is unramified at p, as stated in §1.6 PDF20; the body §9.1 uses that standing local hypothesis.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Algebraic automorphic forms with coefficients
items.statement: For compact open U=U_p U^p and finite O-module W with continuous U_p-action, S(U,W) consists of functions on G(F+)\G(A_f) satisfying f(gu)=u_p^-1 f(g). A sufficiently small level has stabilizer orders prime to p; then S(U,-) is exact and finite over O.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Hecke algebra and attached polarized Galois representation
items.statement: Define the universal unramified Hecke algebra using split places outside S, its image on S(U,W), and localization at a residual eigensystem. Import the associated G_n-valued Galois representation with characteristic polynomial coefficients (-1)^j Norm(w)^(j(j-1)/2) T_w^(j). Define automorphic residual representations by nonzero localized forms.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Modular Serre weight and generic modular weights
items.statement: A weight sigma is modular for residual r at hyperspecial p-level U when S(U,sigma^vee composed with iota_p) localized at r is nonzero. Define W(r) by varying the away-from-p level and W_gen(r) by the generic-weight condition. An automorphic r has at least one such weight by exactness and pro-p invariants.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Geometric and BM Serre weights
items.statement: A geometric weight sigma is one for which the tuple of local residual representations lies on C_sigma. W_gen^g retains (3n-1)-deep weights. W_gen^BM consists of generic weights for which the tuple lies in the support of Z_sigma. It has product structure over p-adic places, and generic geometric weights are BM weights by the unit leading coefficient.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Global weight conjectures
items.statement: The general tame 2n-generic conjecture equates modular weights with W?; the geometric BM conjecture equates generic modular and BM weights for automorphic r. These remain conjectures outside the polynomial-generic theorem below.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Polynomial-generic weight part of Serre's conjecture for U(n)
items.statement: In the standing definite-unitary unramified local setting, with p not dividing 2n, residual r automorphic, r restricted to G_{F(zeta_p)} adequate, and tame local inertia whose chosen lowest-alcove parameters mu are generic for a nonzero integral polynomial P independent of p, W(r)=W_gen^g(r_p)=W?(r_p inertia) and W_gen(r)=W_gen^BM(r_p). Preserve all global hypotheses and do not impose an additional mild-level condition away from p.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Genericity polynomial and global examples
items.statement: Build the sufficient P from the depth, local-model, shifted and component-membership polynomials listed in Remark9.1.7. Enlarging it can make all predicted weights generic. Import the globalization result [14, CorollaryA.7] to realize any allowed semisimple local example in an adequate potentially diagonalizably automorphic global representation.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Geometric weights equal predicted weights generically
items.statement: A nonzero integral polynomial Q built from finitely many shifted fixed-point polynomials P_w, together with the 4n-depth polynomial, makes W_gen^g(rho)=W?(rho inertia) for tame residual L-parameters. The product is finite modulo central translations.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Primes of pulled-back Serre components
items.statement: For sufficiently generic tame rho and (3n-1)-deep sigma, the pullback of C_sigma to the product framed deformation ring is irreducible or zero; define its prime p_sigma(rho), using the unit ideal for an absent component. This requires analytic irreducibility, not merely an irreducible stack component.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Support of any weak detectable patching functor
items.statement: For a suitable polynomial-generic tame rho, a weak detectable patching functor has nonzero weight evaluations exactly on W?(rho inertia), and among generic weights exactly on W_gen^BM(rho). The argument uses defect-lowering types, domains, maximal Cohen–Macaulay support and component primes. No minimal rank-one hypothesis is imposed on this functor.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Modularity lifting from polynomial-generic local domains
items.statement: For a CM extension in the applicable local unramified setting, a continuous r:G_F->GL_n(E) with finite ramification, potentially crystalline regular type (lambda+eta,tau) at p, polynomial-generic tame tau, polarization r^c=r^vee epsilon^(1-n), semisimple residual restrictions at p, adequate residual image on G_{F(zeta_p)} and zeta_p not in F^{ker ad rbar}, and a residual RACSDC automorphic lift with matching weight and K-types, is automorphic with that weight and type. The residual bars were checked in the published PDF image; residual automorphy is the hypothesis, not prior automorphy of r.
items.note: Route owner: PolarizedAutomorphyLifting. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Change-of-weight relaxation of modularity lifting
items.statement: After strengthening the genericity polynomial, the residual automorphic lift in V12 need not initially have matching weight/type: the weight theorem supplies the change of weight. The polynomial is not made effective in arbitrary rank.
items.note: Route owner: PolarizedAutomorphyLifting. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Arbitrary-level patching functor realizing modular weights
items.statement: For p not dividing 2n, automorphic residual r in the standing definite-unitary setting with adequate restriction to G_{F(zeta_p)}, there exists a weak patching functor M_infty such that M_infty(sigma) is nonzero iff sigma belongs to W(r). The construction allows arbitrary away-from-p level after choosing one sufficiently small level realizing all weights.
items.note: Route owner: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIPatchedGLdDensity. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Detectability of the global patching functor
items.statement: If additionally local inertia is tame with parameters generic for P_{6n-2}P_{2eta,e}, the functor in A01 can be taken detectable. This uses upper-alcove obvious-weight nonvanishing followed by the external weight-propagation theorem [56, Theorem4.3.8].
items.note: Route owner: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIPatchedGLdDensity. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Annihilator containment forces covering
items.statement: For a weak patching functor, a (3n-1)-deep sigma0 whose annihilator lies in the component prime p_sigma must cover sigma in the finite-group sense. Type annihilators and the component upper bound establish the implication.
items.note: Route owner: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIPatchedGLdDensity. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Upper-alcove obvious weights occur for weak patching
items.statement: For P_{2eta,e}-generic tame rho and any weak patching functor for rho, every obvious weight in the highest p-restricted alcove has nonzero evaluation. Use a Hodge-2eta domain, maximal Cohen–Macaulay support and the covering criterion; this does not assert all obvious weights for an arbitrary weak functor without the propagation input.
items.note: Route owner: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIPatchedGLdDensity. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Liftings, strict equivalence and abelianized determinant
items.statement: For a continuous residual representation into a split possibly disconnected reductive group, define A-valued liftings over complete Noetherian local O-algebras with residue F, strict conjugacy by the reduction kernel, deformation classes and composition to the abelianized group. These are prerequisites imported once from the deformation owner.
items.note: Route owner: GlobalGaloisDeformations. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Polarized group G_n and multiplier
items.statement: G_n=(GL_n times GL_1) semidirect {1,j}, with j(g,a)j=(a transpose(g)^-1,a), multiplier nu(g,a)=a and nu(j)=-1. Import the abelianization description and the adjoint action used by the global deformation complex.
items.note: Route owner: GlobalGaloisDeformations. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Local deformation problem
items.statement: A nonempty strict-conjugacy-invariant subfunctor of framed local liftings is a local deformation problem when it preserves the specified Artinian fiber products, inverse limits and descent along injective coefficient maps. It is represented by a quotient of the framed deformation ring.
items.note: Route owner: GlobalGaloisDeformations. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Fixed-determinant local deformation quotients
items.statement: Fix a lift xi of the abelianized determinant. Define its framed quotient and then the maximal O-flat quotient. If the residual image lies in the identity component, projection to GL_n identifies the intended fixed-multiplier lifting problem with the GL_n problem; verify the paper's distinction between flat and unrestricted quotients before treating this as a literal ring identity.
items.note: Route owner: GlobalGaloisDeformations. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Polarized global deformation data
items.statement: A datum consists of F/F+, finite ramification set S, O, residual G_n-valued r inducing the quadratic component character, a fixed determinant lift xi and local deformation problems. Absolute irreducibility on G_F gives representability of global deformation classes and their local-condition quotient.
items.note: Route owner: GlobalGaloisDeformations. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Partially framed global deformation rings
items.statement: For T contained in S, introduce frames alpha_v reducing to identity and simultaneous strict equivalence. Construct the representing ring R_S^{square T}, its map from the completed tensor of local rings at T, and the power-series frame comparison after choosing a universal lifting. For a nonempty framing set and p>2 the polarized centralizer is trivial; avoid treating an unframed torsor as canonically trivial.
items.note: Route owner: GlobalGaloisDeformations. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Relative tangent and Selmer complexes
items.statement: Use the relative tangent m/(m^2+varpi A) for maps to F[epsilon]/epsilon^2. Form the global cochain cone with local subcomplexes C^0 and permitted local cocycles L_v at unframed places. The source's displayed tangent identification omits the relative base term and writes all 1-cochains where liftings give 1-cocycles; these are recorded in E22–E23 after image verification. The full Lie algebra of G_n has an additional multiplier summand; identify it with gl_n only for the fixed-multiplier problem.
items.note: Route owner: GlobalGaloisDeformations. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Relative framed tangent comparison
items.statement: The relative tangent space of R_S^{square T} over the tensor of local rings is naturally H^1 of the specified Selmer cone. Its displayed quotient includes the local base maximal ideal; keep this relative statement distinct from the incorrect preceding absolute-looking formula.
items.note: Route owner: GlobalGaloisDeformations. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Taylor–Wiles local deformation condition
items.statement: At a split auxiliary place with norm 1 modulo p, choose a nonzero generalized Frobenius eigenspace on which Frobenius acts semisimply and its stable complement. Lift the complement unramified and require inertia on the selected summand to be scalar. This defines the auxiliary local deformation problem.
items.note: Route owner: GlobalGaloisDeformations. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Adequate Taylor–Wiles prime supply and generator bound
items.statement: For polarized adequate data, odd multiplier at infinity, split places outside T and the stated local tangent dimensions, choose q at least the dual Selmer dimension and a prescribed q0. For each N there is a disjoint split set Q of size q with norms 1 modulo p^N and chosen eigenspaces, making the partially framed ring topologically generated over the local tensor by q-sum_{v in T,v divides p}[F_v+:Q_p]n(n-1)/2 elements.
items.note: Route owner: GlobalGaloisDeformations. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Diamond group and augmentation descent
items.statement: Define Delta_Q as the product of maximal p-quotients of residue-field units at Q. Scalar inertia characters give O[Delta_Q]->R_{S_Q}; quotient by its augmentation ideal recovers the original deformation ring, including the partially framed variant.
items.note: Route owner: GlobalGaloisDeformations. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Auxiliary parahoric levels
items.statement: From the selected eigenspace dimensions form the block parahoric levels U_0(Q), their determinant-kernel levels U_1(Q), and the quotient U_0(Q)/U_1(Q)=Delta_Q. Preserve the chosen split-place identifications and original arbitrary away-from-p level.
items.note: Route owner: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIPatchedGLdDensity. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Local-global compatibility at auxiliary levels
items.statement: For the specified algebraic and Weil–Deligne coefficient type, localized Hecke eigensystems at U, U_0(Q), U_1(Q) carry polarized G_n-valued Galois representations of the listed deformation types, with multiplier epsilon^(1-n)delta_{F/F+}^n and the stated Hecke characteristic polynomials. At U_1(Q) the auxiliary scalar-inertia deformation conditions apply; at U and U_0(Q) they are unramified. Use local Hodge weight lambda+eta and monodromy <=tau, correcting the printed definition as E33–E34 explain.
items.note: Route owner: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIPatchedGLdDensity. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Taylor–Wiles projectors and free diamond modules
items.statement: Sufficient smallness makes S(U_1(Q),W) free over O[Delta_Q], with augmentation invariants equal to S(U_0(Q),W). Commuting local projectors pr_{varpi_v} select a free summand; its augmentation invariants identify with the image of the original-level localized forms. Import the projector and comparison results from [78].
items.note: Route owner: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIPatchedGLdDensity. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Finite patching modules and coefficient power series
items.statement: Define the projected Pontryagin-dual finite modules M_{m,K_p,r}, then adjoin S-frames and quotient augmentation powers to obtain M^square. Choose generators of each auxiliary Delta and maps O[[y_1,...,y_q]] to its group ring. S_infty combines these diamond variables with the frame variables, with fixed augmentation quotient.
items.note: Route owner: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIPatchedGLdDensity. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Ultrafilter patched module
items.statement: Choose a nonprincipal ultrafilter on the auxiliary levels. The localized product of O modulo varpi^r has completion O; use this to form the inverse limit of the tensor of products of finite patching modules. Its augmentation quotient is completed localized automorphic forms. This choice-dependent construction must precede any later independence theorem.
