items.note: Route owner: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIPatchedGLdDensity. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Projectivity and regular sequence of the patched module
items.statement: The diamond and frame variables form an M_infty-regular sequence. The augmentation quotient is projective over O[[G_0(Z_p)]], giving maximal Cohen–Macaulayness and, by [82, Theorem6.2], finite projectivity over S_infty[[G_0(Z_p)]]. No generic rank-one conclusion follows here.
items.note: Route owner: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIPatchedGLdDensity. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Patched deformation ring and its actions
items.statement: Form R_infty=R_loc[[x_1,...,x_g]] with g given by the Taylor–Wiles generator bound, choose maps to finite-level framed rings, and obtain its action on M_infty. Formal smoothness lifts the S_infty-action. The printed g uses [F:Q] where PropositionA.3.3 gives [F+:Q]; use the corrected degree [F+:Q] as recorded in E24.
items.note: Route owner: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIPatchedGLdDensity. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Exact covariant patching functor
items.statement: Set M_infty(W)=Hom_cont,O[[G_0(Z_p)]](M_infty,W^vee)^vee. Projectivity makes it exact and covariant on finite coefficient modules, with finite R_infty- and S_infty-values. For a Serre weight its augmentation quotient identifies with the dual localized automorphic space of dual coefficients.
items.note: Route owner: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIPatchedGLdDensity. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Support and maximal Cohen–Macaulay properties
items.statement: Local-global compatibility forces type evaluations to factor through the appropriate ordered semistable quotient. Dimension equality gives maximal Cohen–Macaulayness there and, for weight constituents, on its special fiber. Nakayama identifies nonzero patched weight values with modular weights. The away-from-p tensor is equidimensional by [5]/[12], and is not asserted formally smooth for arbitrary level.
items.note: Route owner: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIPatchedGLdDensity. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Explicit rank-three monodromy chart
items.statement: For n=3, singleton J, lambda=(3,1,0), z=(23)t_(2,1,1), write the universal determinant-bounded chart matrix and impose det(A)=-(v-t)^4, minor divisibility and reduced closure. Central translation reduces the monodromy parameter to (a,b,0).
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Explicit open genericity locus
items.statement: Use V=Spec Z[a,b,1/P] with P=7! b(b-1)(a-1)(a-2)(a-b)(a-b-1)(a-b-2). Invert all these factors before eliminating variables or asserting normality; the coefficient prime therefore exceeds 7.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Three equations for the explicit chart
items.statement: On V the rank-three chart is presented by the three displayed polynomials in t,a,b,c12,c13,d21,c22,d31,d33, eliminating the other six chart coefficients using monodromy and t-torsion-freeness. The exact three equations are in sourceData.appendixB.chartEquations. Rational-function-field consistency checks are recorded in validation; a uniform localized-integer certificate is a remaining blueprint proof obligation.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Seven special-fiber components
items.statement: On t=0 the chart has the seven component ideals listed in sourceData.appendixB.specialFiberMinimalPrimes. Keep scheme multiplicities distinct from the list of minimal primes; this is not a claim that the original special fiber is reduced.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Complete intersection and flatness of the explicit chart
items.statement: On V the presented chart is an irreducible complete intersection flat over X times V. Fiber codimension three and the regular domain generic fiber identify the presentation with the flat closure.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Effective Elkik Jacobian bound
items.statement: The ideal of 3-by-3 minors of the relative Jacobian of the three-equation presentation contains t^3. The source cites a Macaulay2 computation without a displayed certificate; this needs an independently reproducible polynomial certificate or explicit outstanding proof leaf, not a claimed verified computation.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Partial normalization by an explicit fraction
items.statement: Adjoin W=-t d21/c22 in the fraction field of the chart. The seven displayed relations define the proposed finite birational partial normalization. All statements here are after base change to V, as required by the proposition. The exact seven relations are in sourceData.appendixB.partialNormalizationEquations.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Normal O-flat specialization
items.statement: For a specialization (-p,a,b) in X times V over O, the chart is O-flat and its specified partial normalization is O-flat and normal, hence the normalization. The proof uses a specialized Groebner basis, Cohen–Macaulay leading ideal, generically reduced special fiber, topological flatness and the Pappas–Zhu normality criterion, with regular generic fiber.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Normalization fibers of all seven components
items.statement: Table1 gives the decomposition of the inverse image of each original component, distinguishing the unique maximal-dimensional component from lower-dimensional extras. All seven rows were read in the rotated PDF image and transcribed in sourceData.appendixB.normalizationFiberComponents. The ideals are in the normalization quotient: row four retains its inherited quadratic W equation.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Unibranch fixed point and a dense branching locus
items.statement: For p>7 and all seven parameter factors units, the chart is unibranch at z because its normalization fiber is a singleton. On the component (c22,c13,c12), a generically étale degree-two normalization cover gives a Zariski-dense locus that is not geometrically unibranch. This disproves a blanket all-point unibranch conclusion; distinguish ordinary from geometric unibranchness at nonclosed points.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Explicit depth-ten local comparison in one chart
items.statement: For n=3,K=Q_p,lambda=(3,1,0),z=(23)t_(2,1,1), a 5-generic presentation with mu 10-deep gives the local comparison conclusions in this chart, using Jacobian exponent 3 and m-6+3>6. Use the explicit 10-depth hypothesis: the printed raw polynomial product_{m=0}^{10}(X-Y-m)(Y-Z-m)(Z-X-m) does not imply it, as E26 shows. Alternatively evaluate a signed wall polynomial at mu+eta. Interpret the local isomorphism on the completed framed chart in Theorem7.3.2, retaining its torus torsors.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Product extension of the numerical example
items.statement: Products preserve the reduced special-fiber and normalization facts in this example, giving the analogous chart statement for general unramified K/Q_p and corresponding product data. This is not an arbitrary-product preservation theorem for unibranchness without the stated geometric hypotheses.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Type A equivalued affine Springer fixed points
items.locator: Cited input [1], Boixeda Alvarez arXiv:1910.04780v3 Theorem3.1, PDF5; definitions PDF1–4; used in LLHLM23 Proposition4.7.3.
items.statement: Over C, for the simply connected Type A group with chosen Borel/Iwahori and diagonal regular semisimple s, put gamma=t*s. For w in the fundamental box F of dominant restricted alcoves, let Y_w be the closure of G(C[[t]])wB/B intersect Fl_gamma. Then its T-fixed points are exactly the affine Weyl elements y with y<=w0*w. The GLn central-translation and left/right quotient adapters must be supplied when importing this into LLHLM23; the theorem itself is a characteristic-zero result, and LLHLM23 spreads nonempty intersections to obtain polynomial conditions in characteristic p.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Explicit affine Springer component matrix and inverse
items.locator: Cited input [1], Boixeda Alvarez arXiv:1910.04780v3 AppendixB.2–B.5, PDF8–17; corrected E29–E31.
items.statement: For w in the Type A fundamental box, set a^w_ji to the least k for which w^-1(e_i-e_j)+k*delta is a positive affine root. Construct the lower unitriangular matrix whose ji entry is the sum over increasing paths i=i1<...<ik=j of product_l ((s_il-s_i(l+1))/(s_il-s_ik))*t^(sum_l a^w_i(l+1),il)*product_l A_i(l+1),il. Distinct s_i make all denominators units. The inverse has path coefficient (-1)^(k-1)*product_l (s_il-s_i(l+1))/(s_i1-s_i(l+1)). This gives an affine open in the component and satisfies M^-1*t*s*M in w Lie(B). The fixed-point witness reduces to nonsingular determinant minors; the source degree-maximization algorithm and Vandermonde reductions are explicit further proof leaves, with transversality intersection zero.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.
